They have earned for themselves from their own actions; and you have earned from your own actions.

**The text repeats.**

Should the Jews and the Christians still continue, in their stubbornness, to deny, Allah asks the Holy Prophet and the Muslims to declare in plain and simple words that Allah, being the Lord of All, cannot show any special favour to any particular group of His creatures, and that on the Day of Judgment He will assess the Jews and the Christians as well as the Muslims according to what each has believed in and how each has been behaving - a principle which was accepted by the People of the Book too. The Muslims have also been asked to announce that they on their part recognize no other god but Allah, and have purified their religion of all traces of association (Shirk) - as against the Jews and the Christians who consider Sayyidna Uzayr (Ezra) and Sayyidna Isa (Jesus) respectively to be "the Son of God", and whose religions have, moreover, been abrogated. It so happens with some pious people that once they start seeking this kind of "sincerity" in offering their enjoined prayers, they find that they cannot keep up an unbroken concentration of mind, and are so frightened by this lapse that they sometimes give up offering their prayers, believing such worship to be "insincere" and hence invalid.

**Each person's reward.**

Each person will receive his reward, according to what they themselves do. (And ye will not be asked) on the Day of Judgement (of what they used to do) in this world. The barriers of fate came between you and them for they built their struc tures on separation and heedlessness while you have pitched your tents on closeness and connection. If faith is to be of the kind which pleases God, it must be identical with that of the Companions of the Prophet.

**The faith of the age.**

What was so special about that faith was that it amounted to acceptance of the truth on an abstract level; it was belief in truth for the sake of truth. This had become a rarity in a society which, revering the words of the ancient prophets, regarded as truth whatever had been sanctified by centuries-old tradition. Continued belief in such ‘truth’, embellished as it was by myth and legend, became a matter of national pride; to regard it in any other light would have been to deny a great legacy from the past. The freedman of Our favor ʿatīq faḌlinā is not like the fugitive of Our force Ṭarīd qahrinā.

142.text:
"The foolish among the people will ask, Why did they turn away from the direction of prayer they used to face? Say, O Prophet, The east and west belong only to Allah." opens with a prediction of a question that the foolish will put. The question is about the turning away from the direction the believers used to face in prayer, and the verse gives the question before it gives the answer. The word only places the direction in the hand of the Lord, so no direction has any power of its own. "He guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path" makes the guidance the Lord's choice and not the choice of a direction. The Tanwīr reads the foolish as the ignorant among the Jews and others, and it reads the phrase unto Allah belong the East as a sign that the believers pray toward the Kaʿbah. The Wāḥidī commentary gives an account of the Messenger's turn in the prayer, and the Tazkirul commentary states that the direction is the one God lays down. The phrase "Say, O Prophet" marks the reply as one the Prophet is told to give, so the answer comes from the one who was sent. The verse is short, and the list of its phrases runs in the order the listeners would have heard them. The reader is shown the verse as the first answer to a dispute that the change of direction would bring, and as a reminder that guidance comes from the Lord alone, who gives it to whoever He chooses. The short sentences of the verse are set in the order of a question followed by its answer, so the reader meets the doubt before the reply to it.

**The foolish will ask.**

The fools among the people will say What has turned them from the direction they used to face in their prayersḍ The eyes of the disbelievers were weak so the correct view about all the circumstances of the believers was not apparent to them. (The foolish of the people) the ignorant among the Jews and Arab idolaters (will say: What hath turned them) made them change (from the Qiblah which they formerly observed) except that they want to revert to the religion of their ancestors; it is also said that this means: there was no reason to turn from the direction in which they prayed, i.e. The foolish and weak-minded among the Jews, and those like them from among the hypocrites, will ask what turned the Muslims away from the prayer direction of Bayt al-Maqdis, which was their direction of prayer before. The fools the ignorant among the people that is the Jews and the idolaters will say ‘What matter has turned them the Prophet s and the believers from the direction they were facing in their prayers formerly?’ this being the Holy House bayt al-maqdis sc.

**Why turn away.**

They said that if their qibla was correct what would turn them from itḍ So [God] said: When the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, went to Medina, he prayed toward the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months. But Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, liked to be directed in prayer toward the Ka'bah. In the second year after the Prophet’s emigration to Madīnah, he was commanded to alter the direction of prayer, and face Makkah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis.

**East and West belong to Allah.**

(unto Allah belong the East) praying to the Ka'bah (and the West) the prayer that you prayed in the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis-both are with Allah's command. Tell them, O Prophet, in reply, that to Allah belongs the east and the west and every direction, and He directs whomever He wills of His servants to whatever direction He wills.

**Guidance to the Straight Path.**

He guides whomever He will His guidance being to a straight path’ that is the religion of Islam and you are among these guided ones. He guides whom He wills of His servants to the right path which is free of distortions and misguidance.

**The direction laid down.**

The direction that He lays down is the one that we should face in our prayer, irrespective of what direction it may be. They realized that it was not the direction of prayer that really mattered, but God’s commandment. So, the revealed religions and the Shari'ahs of the prophets the collective name for which is "Islam " - have not shown unnecessary regard to such arbitrary and accidental factors, but have, in determining the principle of integration and unity among men, established themselves on the only basis which can possibly be valid - that is, the unity of mind arising out of doctrinal unity. The first prayer which he offered (facing the Ka'bah) was the 'Asr (Afternoon) prayer in the company of some people.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Bayt al-Maqdis; the sīn of sa-yaqūlu ‘they will say’ denotes the future tense and informs of the Unseen. Say ‘To God belong the East and the West that is all directions. Thus He commands that they face whichever direction He wills and there can be no objection. "Qiblah " signifies the direction to which one turns one's face. It goes without saying that a true Muslim turns in every form of worship towards Allah alone, and Allah is not limited to any particular direction but transcends all dimensions. The logic of this fact requires that in worshipping Him everyone should be free to choose any orientation that he likes, and that he should have the allowance to keep changing his orientation as it suits him. But Divine Wisdom found it more in the fitness of things that all the worshippers should turn to the same direction, and have a fixed orientation. For, worship has several forms, some of which pertain to a single individual, while others have a collective aspect too. Among the first are included fasting, remembrance of Allah (dhikr) etc. which can be performed in privacy, while the Salah and the Hajj are performed openly and in a congregation. The latter, beside being forms of worship, have a secondary function as well - that of providing a social and collective discipline to the Muslims. Obviously, the basic principle of social organization is the unity and integration of the individuals, on the firmness and solidity of which depends the strength of the social organization, whereas an improper emphasis on individuality encourages a disintegrating and fissiparous tendency. As to what the principle of unity and integrity should be, different people have chosen different ways at different times. For example, some have adopted race or colour as the integrating principle, others have opted for the homeland or the geographical region, still others for language. But all these considerations are purely arbitrary and accidental; instead of bringing men together, they divide them, and pro-duce, (as the newspapers show us every day) worldwide concussions. In other words, Islam has called upon men not to become divided in the worship of a thousand false gods, but to join together in the worship of the True God, the One, the Incomparable - the only worship which can draw men from the four corners of the world, men of the past, of the present and of the future, all into a single body of the Faithful. Then, in order to give this inner unity a visible form and also to reinforce it, certain external expressions of unity have also been prescribed. But in both the cases the basic principle has been that the unity in view should not be imposed by circumstances, but arise from an act of will and choice, and produce a spiritual brotherhood. As to the accidental factors like race or colour or birth-place, Islam has given them their proper place in the social life of man, but has not allowed any of them to usurp the central position. It is only in the field where human’ s will can exercise its power to choose that Islam has sought to establish unity among men, internal as well as external. Moreover, the consideration inherent in the relevant injunctions and regulations has been that the things which are to serve as the point of unity should be of such a nature that every human being - man or woman, literate or illiterate, townsman or rustic - can choose and adopt them with equal ease.

143.text:
"And so We have made you believers an upright community so that you may be witnesses over humanity and that the Messenger may be a witness over you" opens with the word upright, which names the community that the Lord has shaped. The community is a witness over humanity, and the Messenger is a witness over the community, so the witness passes from one to the next. The sentence then turns to the direction of prayer: "We assigned your former direction of prayer only to distinguish those who would remain faithful to the Messenger from those who would lose faith." The word only limits the purpose of the former direction to a test, so the direction itself was never the goal. "It was certainly a difficult test except for those rightly guided by Allah." The difficulty is admitted, and the exception is given for those whom Allah guided. "And Allah would never discount your previous acts of faith." This line protects the earlier prayers from loss. "Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity" closes the verse with the mercy that governs the whole change. The Mukhtaṣar gives the sense that Allah chose the direction for them as He chose the Prophet, and that the first change of direction was hard except for the guided. The Tazkirul commentary takes the change of the qiblah as a sign that God had removed the old direction from its place of honour. The Tanwīr reads the former direction as Bayt al-Maqdis and the new one as the Kaʿbah. The reader is asked to see the verse as an account of a community set for witness, tested by a change of direction, and assured that its earlier prayers are not lost.

**An upright community.**

Thus in the same way that We guided you to it We appointed you O community of Muhammad a midmost community excellent and upright that you might be witnesses to the people on the Day of Resurrection that their messengers delivered the Message to them; and that the Messenger might be a witness to you that he delivered the Message to you and We did not appoint make the direction for you now the direction you were facing that is the Ka‘ba the Prophet s used to face it in prayer but when he emigrated he was commanded to face the Holy House of Bayt al-Maqdis in order to win the hearts of the Jews. (Thus) i.e. just as we have honoured you with the Religion of Abraham (Islam) and his direction of prayer (We have appointed you a middle nation) a middlemost community, (that you be witnesses) for the prophets (over mankind, and that the Messenger) Muhammad ﷺ (may be a witness over you) that you are upright and follow the straight path. Just as I made a direction of prayer for you, I have chosen you to be a good, just and balanced nation from among all the communities: in your beliefs and your ways of worship and in your transactions, so that you will be witnesses for the prophets of Allah on the Day of Judgement, confirming that they delivered the messages Allah instructed them to deliver to their people; and so that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ will also witness that he delivered his message to you. Surely God is clement, ever-merciful toward the people.

**The former direction as a test.**

(And We appointed) changed (the Qiblah which ye formerly observed) prayed towards for a period of 19 months (only that We might know) see and distinguish (him who followeth the Messenger) concerning the Qiblah, (from him who turneth) reverts (on his heels) to his former religion and direction of prayer. The first change of prayer direction was difficult, except for those who Allah granted faith to and who were certain that whatever He decrees for His servants has far reaching wisdom and underlying reasons behind it. The change of qiblah was a sign that God had removed the Children of Israel from their position of spiritual leadership and appointed in their place the followers of Muhammad. " (9:30) -, and that on the other hand some people from among them, in spite of having recognized and acknowledged their prophet on the basis of his oft-repeated miracles, refused to obey him when he asked them to take part in a holy war, and bluntly said: ‌ "Go forth, you and your Lord, and fight; we will be sitting here.

**Witnesses over humanity.**

Let us not, however, forget that consensus or Ijma' in this context does not at all imply a sort of referendum on the basis of adult franchise, but means the agreement of a majority of such scholars as fulfil the necessary conditions for pronouncing a judgment in the matters of the Shari'ah - that is to say, those who possess the authority to exercise Ijtihad. What they, however, mean is that obeying someone other than Allah in the course of Salah invalidates it, but if one is actually obeying a divine commandment and the other man is acting only as a means of communicating this injunction to him, it does not invalidate the prayers at all. This is not a reward for superiority but a massive responsibility, so that all of the Muslims’ social and community-based planning must of necessity be dawah-oriented. From among the animals He chose the Adamites, from the Adamites He chose the faithful, from the faithful He chose the prophets, and from the prophets He chose MuḤammad.

**Prayers not discounted.**

Allah will not make you lose your faith in Him, or your good actions, including the prayers you prayed before the change of prayer direction. (But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain) that He thwarts your faith as it was prior to the abrogation of legal rulings; and it is also said that this means: it is not Allah's purpose to thwart your faith but rather His purpose is to abrogate the legal rulings which conduct your faith; and it is also said that this means: Similarly, saying that Allah's Messenger was in the Wasat of his people, means he was from the best subtribe. This is why MuṣṬafā said, "I was brought forth from the best generation of the children of Adam, generation after generation, until I came to be in the generation in which I am.

**Mercy and the change.**

Allah did not thwart your prayers towards Bayt al-Maqdis but He has abrogated the ruling which required you to pray towards Bayt al-Maqdis, (for Allah is full of pity, Merciful) in that He does not thwart your faith as it was before the abrogation of legal rulings (towards mankind) towards the believers. Now the Ka’bah shall remain, until the end of time, the rallying point for the call of divine religion, a centre for all true believers in God, with Muslims acting as a ‘middle nation’ (ummat wasat), or intermediaries, between God and man. It is for them to communicate the word of God to their fellow human beings, just as the Prophet had done in his time. According to this interpretation, Allah assures the Muslims that the commandment changing the Qiblah would in no way affect the validity of the prayers they have been offering so far in the direction of the Baytul-Maqdis - Allah would not allow these prayers to go waste, for they are valid, and have already been accepted.

**What else the same passage holds.**

The verse qualifies the Islamic nation (Ummah) with the objective Wasat which signifies "moderate, middle or central", and is usually applied to a thing considered to be the best of its kind. According to a hadith reported by al-Tirmidhi from the blessed Companion Abu Said al-Khudri the word Wasat is to be interpreted as "just" - in the sense of being "the best" (Qurtubi). The verse points out that just as Allah has granted to the Muslims a Qiblah which is superior to all other orientations, in the same way He has bestowed upon the Islamic Ummah the unparalleled distinction of being moderate, balanced and just - in short, the honour of occupying the central position among all the Ummahs or Traditional communities. This distinction will manifest itself in its full resplendence on the Day of Judgment. Those among the earlier Ummahs who had been denying their prophets would, on that day, pretend that they had never received a book from Allah nor had any prophet given them any kind of guidance.

144.text:
"Indeed, We see you O Prophet turning your face towards heaven" opens with the Lord seeing the Prophet turn his face, which the translation renders as a glance that is already known to Allah. The sentence then gives the promise: "Now We will make you turn towards a direction of prayer that will please you." The word please marks the change as one that the Prophet would welcome, so the verse gives comfort before it gives the command. *"So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, wherever you are, turn your faces towards it."* The command is given to the Prophet and then to all the believers in the same words, so no one is left outside it. "Those who were given the Scripture certainly know this to be the truth from their Lord." The knowledge of the People of the Book is named as a fact that they carry in their own books. "And Allah is never unaware of what they do" closes the verse with the watch of the Lord over their deeds. The Mukhtaṣar states that God will turn the Prophet to a direction which he will be pleased with, and that the Jews and the Christians know the change from their scriptures. The Tazkirul commentary states that the Prophet first made Bayt al-Maqdis his direction, out of faithfulness to the principle of the prophets before him. The Maʿārif commentary takes the turning of the face as the inner desire of the Prophet for the Kaʿbah, so that the command answers a wish that was already in his heart. The reader is shown the change of direction as a command that answers a desire, and a knowledge that the People of the Book already held.

**Turning the face to heaven.**

(We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven (for guidance, O Muhammad) turning your sight to heaven in anticipation of Gabriel coming down to announce the change of the Qiblah. God saw you, O Prophet, turning your face and gazing towards the heavens, anticipating revelation about changing the direction of prayer to the place you loved. We have seen thy face turning about in heaven.

**A direction that will please you.**

We have indeed qad ‘indeed’ is for affirmation seen you turning your face about in the direction of the heaven looking around for the Revelation and longing for the command to face the Ka‘ba he the Prophet wished for this because it was the prayer-direction of Abraham and would be more conducive to the submission of the Arabs to Islam; now We will surely turn you to a direction that shall satisfy you that you will love. (And now surely We shall make thee turn (in prayer) toward a Qiblah that is dear to thee) that you like, namely, the Qiblah of Abraham. God will turn you to a prayer direction which you will be pleased with, to the Sacred House of God, instead of the prayer direction you now face, so turn your face to the Sacred House of God in Makkah, and wherever you are, O believers, turn towards it to perform your prayers. Faithful to this principle, he initially made Bayt al-Maqdis his prayer direction, or the qiblah, for prophets since the time of Solomon had prayed in that direction.

**The Sacred Mosque.**

(So turn thy face) when in prayer (towards the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be) whether on land or in the sea, (turn your faces (when ye pray) in prayer (towards it. (Lo! Those who have received the Scripture know that) the Sacred Precinct (is the Truth from their Lord) is the Qiblah of Abraham but they conceal this fact. (And Allah is not unaware) heedless (of what they do) of what they conceal. (...so turn your face in the direction of Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah).) means its direction." The situation required that the Holy Qur'an should use the phrase: 'Turn your face toward the Ka'bah or toward the Baytullah .' But we actually find the Holy Qur'an saying:

**Those who know the truth.**

Those who have been given the Scripture know that it the change towards the Ka‘ba is the fixed truth from their Lord on account of the description in their Scripture of how the Prophet s would re-orient himself to it; God is not heedless of what you do O believers when you obey His command alternatively ta‘malūna ‘you do’ can be read ya‘malūna ‘they do’ in other words it would be referring to the Jews’ denial of the matter concerning the direction of prayer. Those who have been given the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians, know well that the change of prayer direction is the truth revealed from their Creator Who arranges and manages their lives, as it is clear in their Scripture. The prophets who hailed from among the Jewish people had been informed that one day God would alter the qiblah, and they had passed the knowledge on to the Jews. This verse begins by speaking of how deeply the Holy Prophet ; wished that the Ka'bah be appointed as the Qiblah of the Muslims.

**The watch of the Lord.**

This is why Allah threatened them when He said: Immediately after the promise, there follows the commandment: ‌ ‌ : .Now turn your face in the direction of the Sacred Mosque. So, the word itself points to the rule that in the case of places which are far from Makkah it is not even necessary for the prayers to be valid that one should turn exactly towards Al-Masjid al-Harm for, it is quite sufficient to turn only "in the direction" of the Sacred Mosque, as the Holy Qur'an itself.has indicated.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Turn your face in prayer towards the Sacred Mosque that is the Ka‘ba and wherever you are addressing the Muslim community turn your faces in prayer towards it. This inclination has been explained in different ways, but there is no real contradiction involved in these different views. For example, it has been said that before prophethood was conferred on him, he used to follow, out of the impulsion of his own nature, the way of Sayyidna Ibrahim (Araham) , and that when he began to receive the Revelation, the Holy Qur'an itself designated his Shari'ah as being in total accord with the Abrahamic Way. Moreover, the Qiblah of Sayyidna Ibrahim as well as that of Sayyidna Ismail had been the Ka'bah . So, it was quite in the nature of things for him to wish that the Ka'bah be appointed as the Qiblah of the Muslims. An additional factor was that the Arab tribes, in spite of being associators, at least claimed to be the followers of the Abrahamic Way, and acknowledged the Ka'bah as their Qiblah in contradiction to the Jews. Once the Ka'bah had been made the Qiblah of the Muslims, the Arabs could be expected to find Islam more acceptable. As. for the hope that the adoption of the Baytul-Maqdis as the Qiblah would bring the Jews closer to Islam, it had been dashed by the events of the last sixteen or seventeen months, for the hostility of the Jews to Islam, fed by their vanity, had only been growing more intense. Whatever be the motive, the Holy Prophet was very keen to see the Ka'bah appointed as the Qiblah. Now, prophets are as close to Allah as man can ever be, and this exalted station teaches them to observe a very strict spiritual etiquette - they never submit a request before Allah until and unless they have received the permission to do so. This principle leads us to believe that the Holy Prophet had already been allowed to pray for his wish to be fulfilled, and that he hoped his prayer would be granted. So, he used to turn his face again and again to the sky, anxiously waiting for an angel to appear and bring the injunction he had been wishing for. In the present verse, Allah describes this state of the Holy Prophet in an appreciative manner, and promises to assign him a Qiblah that he would like. " Here we find a manifestation of the subtle workings of divine grace - the Holy Prophet was, to begin with, granted the joy of hearing a promise made, and, immediately after, the greater joy of seeing the promise fulfilled.

145.text:
"Even if you were to bring every proof to the People of the Book, they would not accept your direction of prayer, nor would you accept theirs" opens with a hypothetical that closes off the hope of agreement. The verse sets the case at its most generous, a proof for every question, and it still keeps the two sides apart will not meet. "Nor would any of them accept the direction of prayer of another." The refusal runs in every direction, so neither community accepts the other. "And if you were to follow their desires after all the knowledge that has come to you, then you would certainly be one of the wrongdoers." The warning is placed on the Prophet himself, and the word certainly makes the consequence firm. The turn from knowledge to desire is the wrong that the verse names. The Mukhtaṣar states that if the Prophet left guidance and followed their desires he would be doing wrong, and that God addresses the Prophet directly to show how the believers should stand. The Maʿārif commentary takes the verse as describing a double malice on both sides of the dispute. The Tanwīr gives the sense that the People of the Book would not follow any direction but their own. The Qushayrī commentary states that devotion to the path of the Real was already the Prophet's from the first. The word still in the translation marks the refusal as one that does not end with the proofs, so the verse keeps the question open and leaves the choice with the listeners. The reader is asked to see the verse as a fixed position, and a warning that binds even the Prophet to the knowledge he was given.

**Every proof and no agreement.**

And even if you were to bring to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) all the Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), they would not follow your Qiblah (prayer direction), nor are you going to follow their Qiblah. (And even if thou broughtest unto those who have received the Scripture all kinds of portents) all the signs they asked of you, (they would not follow your Qiblah) they would not pray towards your Qiblah nor embrace your Religion, (nor canst thou be a follower of their Qiblah) nor can you pray towards the Qiblah of the Jews or Christians; (nor are some of them followers of others) nor are some of them going to pray towards the Qiblah of the Jews and Christians. If you provided the Jews and Christians who have been given the Scripture with every sign and proof that the change of prayer direction was the truth, they would not face your prayer direction, stubborn against what you say and too proud to follow the truth. Yet if you should bring to those who have been given the scripture every sign they will not follow your direction and you are not a follower of their direction; neither are they followers of one another's direction.

**Neither direction accepted.**

It is not that they demand solid and convincing arguments in order to be able to accept the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah : it is sheer stubbornness which does not allow them to give their assent, and no proof in the world, declares the Holy Qur'an, is ever going to satisfy them. In fact, their two groups display an equal malice even towards each other - the Jews have adopted the Baytul-Maqdis as their Qiblah while the Christians have chosen the East, and each group rejects the Qiblah of the other. The reason for the majority’s refusal to follow the Prophet was the fact that they were used to behave as they wished. You will not face their prayer direction after God has directed you away from it, and they will not face the prayer directions of one another, because each group calls the other disbelievers, and because they follow their desires in the matter of the prayer direction and in other sacred laws and rulings, even after the true knowledge which was revealed to you and about which there is no doubt.

**Desires after knowledge.**

Verily, if you follow their desires after that which you have received of knowledge (from Allah), then indeed you will be one of the wrongdoers. (And if thou shouldst follow their desires) after being warned and pray towards their Qiblah (after the knowledge which hath come unto you) that the Sacred Precinct is the Qiblah of Abraham, (then surely) if you do that then surely (wert thou of the evil-doers) who harm themselves.

**The wrongdoers.**

Allah describes the Jews' disbelief, stubbornness and defiance of what they know of the truth of Allah's Messenger , that if the Prophet brought forward every proof to the truth of what he was sent with, they will never obey him or abandon following their desires. Naturally, it is impossible for the Holy Prophet g to follow the desires of the People of the Book. Here God addresses the Prophet directly to show how wrong it would be to follow them. Devotion to the path of the Real was already yours from the eternal decree [just as it was decreed] that your enemies would fall to the side.

**Malice on both sides.**

In continuing the discussion on the subject of the Qiblah or the divinely-ordained orientation, the present verse provides yet another instance of the maliciousness of the People of the Book . The prophets who hailed from among the Jewish people had been informed that one day God would alter the qiblah, and they had passed the knowledge on to the Jews. They had certain romantic notions about the special position occupied by their own people, and they had made these the bedrock of their life and creed. They will not follow your qibla even if you were to show them evidence that was clearer than suns and moons.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Yet if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you should bring to those who have been given the Scripture every sign about your truthfulness in the matter of the direction of prayer they will not follow your direction out of obduracy and you are not a follower of their direction this is a categorical negation of his the Prophet’s desire that they become Muslims and of their desire that he return to their direction of prayer; neither are they the Jews and the Christians followers of one another’s direction. If you were to follow their whims the ones to which they summon you after the knowledge the revelation that has come to you then you if hypothetically you were to follow them will surely be among the evildoers. On the other hand, the Holy Prophet , cannot accept either of these two orientations, for the new Qiblah of the Muslims - the Baytullah - has been instituted by a divine commandment, and is never going to be abrogated. So, there is no likelihood of an agreement between the People of the Book and the Muslims in this matter. The Baytul-Maqdis no doubt, had once been instituted by a divine commandment, but that commandment has now been abrogated. Anyone who follows an abrogated injunction, and ignores the new in-junction which has replaced the earlier one, is actually disobeying Allah, and acting upon his individual opinion and personal desire. But, supposing for the sake of supposition, were he to do so even after having received a definite injunction through the Wahy (Revelation), he would be counted among the unjust - that is, among those who disobey divine commandments. Being a prophet, he is essentially sin-less, and as such cannot possibly be among the unjust. From this principle it logically follows that it is impossible for him to favour the desires of the People of the Book, and to accept their Qiblah as his own. Let us make it quite clear that this warning is outwardly addressed to the Holy Prophet but is, in fact, intended for his Ummah, which is being asked to realize fully the gravity of the sin of ignoring or disobeying the injunction which has finally established the Baytullah as the Qiblah of the Muslims. "You are not to follow their Qiblah ", it is meant to declare that the Baytullah shall now stay as the Qiblah upto the end of the world.

146.text:
"Those We have given the Scripture recognize this Prophet as they recognize their own children." opens with a comparison of knowledge to family. The recognition is as close as a father knows his own children, and the verse makes that the measure of what the People of the Book know. "Yet a group of them hides the truth knowingly." The turn comes with the word yet, and the hiding is of the truth that they know. The word knowingly removes any excuse that the concealment was made in ignorance. The verse is placed after the warning against following their desires, so the knowledge that the Prophet was given and the knowledge the People of the Book hold are set side by side. The Mukhtaṣar states that the scholars of the Jews and the Christians hide the truth that has come to them. The Tanwīr turns to the believers among the People of the Book, so that the group that hides is set against a group that accepts. The Maʿārif commentary treats the recognition as irrefutable evidence drawn from their own scriptures. The Tazkirul commentary states that those who do not make the truth their own show that they have rejected it in their hearts. The Wāḥidī commentary links the verse to the believers among the People of the Book, who knew the Messenger and bore witness to him. The reader is asked to see the verse as a charge against concealment, which is the hardest of the errors because it is done with knowledge.

**Recognised as one knows children.**

Those to whom We have given the Scripture they recognise him Muhammad as they recognise their sons because of the descriptions of him in their Scripture ‘Abd Allāh Ibn Salām said ‘I recognised him the moment I saw him as I would my own son; but my recognition of Muhammad was more intense’; even though there is a party of them that conceal the truth that is his description while they know this truth which you Muhammad follow. Then Allah mentions the believers of the people of the Book, saying: The scholars of the Jews and the Christians to whom Allah gave the scripture recognise Muhammad ﷺ as completely as they recognise their own children and distinguish them from others. Those to whom We have given the Scripture they recognize him as they recognize their sons; even though there is a party of them that conceal the truth while they know.

**A group that hides the truth.**

But verily, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it [i.e., the qualities of Muhammad which are written in the Tawrah and the Injil This is) the truth from your Lord. Nevertheless, a group of them hide the truth that has come to them, out of envy, fully aware that it is the truth. (But lo! A party of them) of the people of the Book (knowingly) knowing it to exist in their Book (conceal the Truth) conceal the description and traits of Muhammad ﷺ. The Jews know that the Prophet is True, but they hide the Truth.

**Evidence from their own books.**

On the basis of the irrefutable evidence provided by their own Sacred Books, the Jews and the Christians knew him to be the promised Last Prophet but many of them refused to acknowledge him as such out of sheer obstinacy. As everyone knows, in bringing two terms into comparison with each other, a simile does not involve in this analogy all the aspects of these two terms, but only those which should be relevant to the occasion. Some of them, while denying the truth themselves, even tried to keep it concealed from others, although they knew fully well that this particular truth (that is to say, the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah) had been established by Revelation from Allah Himself. Those who do not make the truth their own, show that they had never realised God, for, if they had, they would have recognized His word when they heard it.

**Believers among the People of the Book.**

This was revealed about the believers of the people of the Book: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions. They knew Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, by his description, traits and mission from their Scripture as did any one of them know his son upon seeing him with other boys. I knew Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, better than I knew my son . 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asked him: Because I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah truly and out of certainty, but I cannot bear witness truly and out of certainty that my son is mine, for I have no knowledge of what women do [behind their husbands' backs] . 'Umar then said:

**Knowledge and concealment.**

No one can then fail to recognize it to be the truth. Those who find words to reject the truth think that they have discovered strong arguments to justify their stand. But very soon they realize that those words were nothing but imaginary props, which they themselves had devised to give false satisfaction to their egos. Their hidden envy causes haughtiness in them concerning what they necessarily know.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Verses 144 and 145 have told us how the People of the Book knew in their hearts that a divine commandment itself had instituted the Baytullah as the Qiblah of the Muslims, and yet denied this fact in public. Now, the two present verses show that their conduct towards the Holy Prophet was equally dishonest and malicious. The Torah and the Evangel had already foretold the coming of the Holy Prophet and set down the signs and indications which should help the people to recognize him. Let us add a word or two in order to explain the simile employed here by the Holy Qur'an - that of man recognizing his own son without any doubt or ambiguity. So, in considering the present simile one should not allow one's imagination to roam far afield, and bring under discussion even those cases which happen to be illegitimate.

147.text:
"This is the truth from your Lord, so do not ever be one of those who doubt." opens with the truth that comes from the Lord, and the verse makes the truth the source of the command. The phrase from your Lord places the truth above any human opinion, and the command that follows is addressed to the Prophet. The word doubt names the state that the Prophet is forbidden to enter. The command is short, so its weight rests on the clear origin of the truth. The Mukhtaṣar takes the verse as a call to make absolute certainty the rule of the heart. The Tanwīr reads the doubt as the wavering of those who are not sure whether they are right. The Maʿārif commentary takes the phrase that the truth is from your Lord as capable of more than one reading, and it draws out the sense that the believer must not be shaken. The Tazkirul commentary states that whenever God reveals some truth to the world, it is the sign of a change in the affairs of the faith. The reader is asked to hold the verse as the answer to the disputes of the earlier verses, and as a warning against the doubt that those disputes can bring.

**The truth from your Lord.**

The truth comes from your Lord; then be not among the doubters who doubt it that is to say ‘be not of such a disposition’ which is more eloquent than merely saying ‘do not waver’. (It is the Truth from thy Lord (O Muhammad) that you are a Prophet sent by Allah. The truth comes from your Lord; then be not among the doubters. i.e. 'after the suns of certainty have appeared to you do not yield to the results of mere guessing'.

**Do not be among those who doubt.**

(So be not thou of those who waver) who doubt whether they know or not. The address is to [the Prophet] but what is intended by it is the community. Whenever God reveals some truth to the world, it is supported by clear arguments.

**Concealment and its opposite.**

But verily, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it [i.e., the qualities of Muhammad which are written in the Tawrah and the Injil This is) the truth from your Lord. The Jews know that the Prophet is True, but they hide the Truth. Allah states that the scholars of the People of the Scripture know the truth of what Allah's Messenger was sent with, just as one of them knows his own child, which is a parable that the Arabs use to describe what is very apparent. Those who do not make the truth their own, show that they had never realised God, for, if they had, they would have recognized His word when they heard it.

**The phrase from your Lord.**

The phrase, "The Truth is from your Lord", can also be interpreted in a general sense as providing a definition of the nature of truth - namely, that alone is truth which comes from Allah. One who has understood this fact can never allow himself to be in doubt with regard to this particular truth or to any other which has been revealed to a prophet by Allah. As everyone knows, in bringing two terms into comparison with each other, a simile does not involve in this analogy all the aspects of these two terms, but only those which should be relevant to the occasion. Some of them, while denying the truth themselves, even tried to keep it concealed from others, although they knew fully well that this particular truth (that is to say, the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah) had been established by Revelation from Allah Himself.

**Words of rejection.**

Those who find words to reject the truth think that they have discovered strong arguments to justify their stand. But very soon they realize that those words were nothing but imaginary props, which they themselves had devised to give false satisfaction to their egos. Some of them, while denying the truth themselves, even tried to keep it concealed from others, although they knew fully well that this particular truth (that is to say, the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah) had been established by Revelation from Allah Himself.

148.text:
"Everyone turns to their own direction of prayer." opens with the statement that each community has a direction it faces, and that the direction is a matter of each people's own choosing. The sentence leaves room for difference, but it does not make the difference a source of division. "So compete with one another in doing good." The command turns the difference of directions into a race in good deeds, so the believers are to outdo one another in what is right. "Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together for judgment." The gathering is set for the Day of Judgement, and the place of the believer does not change the gathering. "Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything" closes the verse with the power that makes the gathering certain. The Mukhtaṣar states that there is nothing wrong with the believers facing different directions, and that Allah will bring them together from wherever they may be. The Tanwīr gives the sense that each adherent of a religion has a goal, and that Allah is able to do all things, including the gathering. The Tazkirul commentary takes the Kaʿbah as the direction of the believers, and it treats the change of qiblah as a change in the sign that marks them. The verse keeps both the difference and the gathering in view, so neither is lost. The reader is asked to see the verse as a command to race in good deeds, and a promise that the race will end in one gathering.

**Everyone turns to their own direction.**

Every person of every community has his direction wijha his qibla to which he turns muwallīhā ‘he turns to it’ is also read as muwallāhā ‘he is made to turn to it’ in his prayers so vie with one another in good works strive with acts of obedience and acceptance of these. (And each one hath a goal) to each adherent of a religion a Qiblah (towards which he turneth) he faces according to his own whim; it is also said that this means: to each prophet a Qiblah, which is the Ka'bah, towards which he is ordered to face; (so vie with one another in good works) so hasten, O community of Muhammad, to perform acts of obedience more than any other nation. For this reason, there is a difference between them in their directions of prayer and in their sacred laws. One of them has said that the allusion here is this:

**Compete in doing good.**

There is nothing wrong with them facing different directions if it is by Allah’s command and law, so try to outdo each other, O believers, in doing the good actions that you have been instructed to do. When the Ka‘bah in Makkah was appointed as the prayer direction, or qiblah, the People of the Book started discussing whether the East was God’s direction or the West. Before we leave the subject, let us remark that nowadays quite a good number of people, especially those with a Western formation, approach the Holy Qur'an as they do a book composed by a human author who pays due regard to what commonly passes as logic and sequential argument, and often do feel embarrassed or confused when they come across the close repetition of words and phrases in the Book of Allah, finding it impossible to explain or justify what is seemingly redundant. Then you will go straight in follow ing the Sunnah and conduct of MuṣṬafā and you will perform the rightful due of emulating that paragon of the world.

**Gathered wherever you are.**

Wherever you may be God will bring you all together gathering you on the Day of Resurrection and requiting you for your deeds; surely God has power over all things. (Wheresoever you may be) on land or at sea, (Allah will bring you all together) gather you together and reward you for the good works you performed. Allah will bring you together from wherever you may be on the Day of Judgement, to reward you according to what you have done.

**The power of Allah.**

(Lo! Allah is Able to do all things) like gathering you together as well as other things. It is not difficult for Him to bring you all together and reward you. (Wheresoever you may be, Allah will bring you together (on the Day of Resurrection). Truly, Allah is able to do all things.) meaning: (To each among you, We have prescribed a law and a clear way. If Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but that may test you in what He has given you; so compete in good deeds. The return of you is to Allah.)(5:48)

**One direction and one gathering.**

They saw the matter as one of direction alone, but this was nothing other than sheer ignorance on their part. The selection of the House of God as the qiblah was not merely the specification of a certain direction for prayer; it was a sign that the time had come for God to reveal His greatest favour to man. The change of qiblah, rather than denoting a change from one direction of worship to another, more sacred one, showed the completion of God’s guidance to mankind. So, the verse ends with the rejoinder that on the Day of Judgment Allah shall bring all men together, and suggests that the desire to be safe from the criticism of others and the anxiety to win over them in disputes only betrays one's attachment to the temporal world, and that wisdom lies in caring more for what is everlasting.

**What else the same passage holds.**

The question of religious orientation being of the highest significance for an Ummah (or a traditional community), these verses continue and enlarge upon the theme of the Qiblah, and lay down further raisons d'etre for the change. It is, the commentators point out, an observable fact that every traditional community has had a religious orientation of its own, whether appointed by Allah or chosen by itself. This being so, why should anyone object, or wonder that Allah has appointed for the Islamic Ummah a Qiblah peculiar to it? After all, it is a regular and distinct Tradition in its own right - in fact, the last of all Traditions, which makes it all the more necessary that it must have a distinct Qiblah. Anyhow, once the divine commandment has been promulgated, the Muslims need not worry about the objections or the ridicule of others, but should, above all, concern themselves with the performance of good deeds (as defined by Allah and His Prophet). They should, indeed, give up fruitless controversies and strive to excel in good deeds, for they have to appear before Allah on the Day of Judgment when they will be rewarded or punished according to their deeds. The raison d'etre laid down in this verse requires that the Muslims should, whether staying at home or travelling, turn their faces in the direction of Al-Masjid al-Harm for that undoubtedly is the Qiblah appointed for them by divine commandment. It is obligatory for them to obey this as well as any other commandment, bearing in mind that Allah is not unaware of what men do.

149.text:

**Wherever you are.**

(And whencesoever you comest forth (for prayer, O Muhammad) turn thy face) in prayer (towards the Inviolable Place of Worship; Lo! It) the Inviolable Place of Worship (is the Truth from your Lord) it is the Qiblah of Abraham, Allah bless him.

From whatever place you issue on a journey turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; it is the truth from your Lord. 150.text:
"Wherever you are O Prophet, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque." opens with the command for the Prophet, and the second clause extends it to the believers: "And wherever you believers are, face towards it." The command reaches every believer in the same words, so the direction is the same across all the places they may be. "So that people will have no argument against you, except the wrongdoers among them." The purpose is set out as the removal of argument, and the exception marks the wrongdoers who will argue anyway. "Do not fear them; fear Me, so that I may continue to perfect My favour upon you and so you may be rightly guided." The verse moves from the people who argue to the Lord who is to be feared, and it ends with the favour that is perfected and the guidance that follows. The Mukhtaṣar states that they will remain in their stubbornness and keep arguing with the Prophet, and that he is to fear his Lord alone. The Qushayrī commentary takes perfection to be the addition of unveiling to the blessing. The Jalālayn gives the sense that the contentions of the opponents will cease in this way. The Tazkirul commentary states that God had revealed true religion time and time again, and that the change of direction is the final form of that revelation. The Maʿārif commentary links the verse to the earlier commandment, which concerned the same direction. The sentence keeps the command and its reason together, so the believers see why the direction matters. The reader is asked to see the verse as a close to the matter of the direction, in which fear of the Lord replaces the fear of opponents.

**Wherever you are.**

From whatever place you issue turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you may be turn your faces towards it all of which is being repeated for emphasis so that there be not any argument from the people the Jews or the idolaters against you so that there be not any cause for contention regarding the change to a different direction of prayer. Wherever you come from, O Prophet, when you want to pray, turn towards the direction of the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you may be, O believers, turn your face towards it if you want to pray, so that the people will have no argument against you, except those of them who are wrongdoers. And from wheresoever you start forth (for prayers), turn your face in the direction of Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah), that is indeed the truth from your Lord. The perfection of grace is to add unveiling kashf to kindness luṭf.

**No argument against you.**

In this way their contentions against you will cease to exist both the contentions of the Jews when they say ‘He Muhammad rejects our religion but follows our direction of prayer’ and of the idolaters when they say ‘He Muhammad claims to follow the creed of Abraham but he contravenes his Abraham’s qibla’; excepting the evildoers among them acting in obstinacy who will say ‘He Muhammad only changed to this direction because of his natural inclination towards the idolatrous religion of his forefathers’. They will remain in their stubbornness, arguing against you with the weakest of arguments. Thus, the commandment in Verse 144 pertains to the situation of those who find themselves in Madīnah or in their own home-town, whatever that might be, and is intended to make it clear that the injunction is not particular to the mosque of the Holy Prophet but applies to every town or village and to every quarter of a town.

Do not fear them, but fear your Lord alone, following His instructions and keeping away from what He has prohibited. 151.text:
"Since We have sent you a messenger from among yourselves" opens with a comparison to the prayer that was answered, and the sending is set as a favour that completes the earlier one. The word messenger is the central thing, since the sender is the Lord and the one sent is from among the believers. "Reciting to you Our revelations, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you never knew." The four tasks are given in order: recitation, purification, teaching of the Book and wisdom, and teaching of what was unknown. Each task is named as a gift, and the list closes with the knowledge that they never had before. The verse is the completion of the prayer in the second chapter, which asked for the messenger, and so the reader sees the answer to that request in these four tasks. The Mukhtaṣar takes the sending as a blessing given to the believers in another way. The Qushayrī commentary states that the sending of the messenger was to open the gates of the knowledge of God. The Tazkirul commentary states that the coming of the final prophet was the answer to the prayer made at the building of the Kaʿbah. The Maʿārif commentary lists the same tasks in its own order and treats them as the work of the Prophet among the people. The reader is asked to see the verse as the answer to the prayer of Abraham, which asked for a messenger to recite, teach, and purify.

**A messenger from among yourselves.**

As also We have sent this verbal clause ka-mā arsalnā ‘as We have sent’ is semantically connected to wa-li-utimma of the previous verse that is to say ‘Also We have sent by way of perfection’; as it My grace has been perfected by Our sending among you of yourselves Muhammad a messenger to recite Our verses the Qur’ān to you and to purify you to cleanse you from idolatry and to teach you the Book the Qur’ān and wisdom the rulings therein and to teach you what you knew not. (Even as We have sent unto you a Messenger) remember Me as I have sent a Messenger (from among you) from your own lineage, (who reciteth unto you Our revelations) i.e. the Qur'an: its commands and prohibitions (and causeth you to grow) cleanses you of sin through divine Oneness, the poor-due, and alms, (and teacheth you the Scripture) the Qur'an (and wisdom) the lawful and the prohibited, (and teacheth you) of legal rulings, legal punishments and stories of bygone nations (that which ye knew not) before the revelation of the Qur'an and the advent of Muhammad ﷺ. Allah blessed you in another way: sending a messenger to you from among you, who recites His verses, purifying you by directing you to virtue and goodness and forbidding you from evil and wrong, teaching you the Qur’ān and the Sunnah, and teaching you worldly and sacred knowledge which you did not know.

**Recitation and purification.**

He recites to them the verses of the Qur'an; He teaches them the Book and the wisdom; He purifies them; He teaches them things which his listeners did not know of, nor could they be found in the earlier Divine Books or through individual reason. Similarly (to complete My blessings on you), We have sent among you a Messenger (Muhammad) of your own, reciting to you Our verses (the Qur'an) and purifying you, and teaching you the Book (the Qur'an) and the Hikmah (i. e., Sunnah, Islamic laws and Fiqh jurisprudence), and teaching you that which you did not know Therefore remember Me (by praying, glorifying). Allah reminds His believing servants with what He has endowed them with by sending Muhammad as a Messenger to them, reciting to them Allah's clear Ayat and purifying and cleansing them from the worst types of behavior, the ills of the souls and the acts of Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era). Now, Verse 151 declares that similarly the second request has also been granted, suggesting that since the Holy Prophet has been sent in answer to the prayer of the founder of the Ka'bah it is no wonder that it should be appointed as his Qiblah .

**Teaching the Book and wisdom.**

The Messenger also takes them away from the darkness (of disbelief) to the light (of faith) and teaches them the Book, the Qur'an, and the Hikmah (i.e., the wisdom), which is his Sunnah. (Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger (Muhammad) from among themselves, reciting unto them His verses (the Qur'an), and purifying them (from sins).)(3:164) It was at the time of the construction of the Ka‘bah that Abraham and Ishmael prayed for a prophet to be born among the people of Makkah. The sending of the Messenger was to open the gates of attainment for it was in His prior knowledge that the hearts of His friends would be thirsty to meet Him.

**Teaching what you never knew.**

But, according to al-Qurtubi, the word Kaf or "as" is connected with the first phrase of Verse 152 -: The prayer was answered, and the coming of the final prophet, whose focus would be Makkah, was decreed. As for the sincere—they needed no further proof, but even the conclusiveness of this sign was not enough to silence those who gave no thought to God. What a difference between one people and another!

**The answer to the prayer.**

He had, as one would recall, prayed Allah to accept his founding of the Ka'bah and to send among his progeny a Messenger from among themselves. God’s messengers who came to the world used to prophesy his coming. There is no way for anyone to [reach God] except through the intermediary of the messengers. (Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger (Muhammad) from among themselves, reciting unto them His verses (the Qur'an), and purifying them (from sins).)(3:164)

**What else the same passage holds.**

These verses conclude the discussion on the theme of the Qiblah or religious orientation. So, Verse 151 repeats the second part of the prayer of Sayyidna Ibrahim with which the discussion had begun (Verses 127 - 129). The subsequent discussion on the subject of the Qiblah has already shown that the first prayer has been heard and accepted. Verse 151 has specifically mentioned that the new Prophet (Muhammad) is sent with the same attributes as specified by Sayyidna Ibrahim in his prayer, namely: Since Allah has, in granting the two prayers, sent such great blessings to mankind, Verse 152 asks men to "remember" Him as the Supreme Benefactor, and to render Him thanks by being obedient.

152.text:
"Remember Me; I will remember you." opens with a command to remember the Lord, and the answer is given in the same sentence: the Lord will remember them. The exchange of remembrance is set in a single line, so the command and the promise are read together. "And thank Me, and never be ungrateful." The second command joins gratitude to remembrance, and the word never closes the door on ingratitude. The verse is short, and it places the believers in a relation of mutual remembrance with their Lord. The Mukhtaṣar states that the believers are to remember Allah with their hearts and their whole beings, and to be grateful for the blessings He has given them. The Tanwīr reads the remembrance as the performance of acts of worship, and the thanks as gratitude for the blessings bestowed. The Maʿārif commentary states that remembrance essentially pertains to the heart, and that a mechanical recital alone is not enough. The Tazkirul commentary links the verse to the sincere, who needed no further proof. The reader is asked to see the verse as the close of the passage, in which the believers are bidden to remember and to give thanks, and in which the Lord promises to remember them in return.

**Remember Me.**

So remember Me through prayer glorification and the like I will remember you this is said to mean ‘I will reward you’; in a hadīth about God that He says ‘whoever remembers Me in himself I will remember him in Myself and whoever remembers Me in an assembly I will remember him in an Assembly more excellent than his’; and be thankful to Me for My grace by being obedient and be not ungrateful towards Me through disobedience. (Therefore remember Me) through the performance of acts of obedience, (I will remember you) by granting you Paradise; and it is also said that this means: remember Me in time of ease, I will remember you in times of hardship. So, remember Allah with your hearts and your whole beings, and He will remember you with approval and protection, for you are rewarded according to what you do. You will remember Me when you have tried out the others.

**I will remember you.**

(Therefore remember Me. I will remember you), "Remember Me regarding what I have commanded you and I will remember you regarding what I have compelled Myself to do for your benefit (i.e., His rewards and forgiveness)." (Allah the Exalted said, 'O son of Adam! If you mention Me to yourself, I will mention you to Myself. If you mention Me in a gathering, I will mention you in a gathering of the angels (or said in a better gathering). If you draw closer to Me by a hand span, I will draw closer to you by forearm's length. If you draw closer to Me by a forearm's length, I will draw closer to you by an arm's length. And if you come to Me walking, I will come to you running).

**Thank Me.**

(Give thanks to Me) for the blessings I bestowed upon you, (and reject not Me) do not stop giving thanks for these blessings. Also, be grateful to Allah for the blessings He has given you, and do not be ungrateful by denying them or using them in prohibited ways. Dhikr : or "Remembrance" essentially pertains to the heart, but in so far as the tongue is the interpreter of the heart the oral recitation of a Divine Name or a verse of the Holy Qur'an is also described as Dhikr . One must, however, bear in mind that even a mechanical Dhikr without the heart being engaged in it is not altogether futile.

**Remembrance of the heart.**

He replied that, according to the promise made in the Holy Qur'an, when a Muslim remembers Allah, He too remembers him, and thus everyone can know for himself that as soon as he turns to Allah and remembers Him, Allah too remembers him. Let us add that Verse 152 means to say that if men "remember" Allah by obeying His commandments, He will "remember" them by granting His pardon and His rewards. I'm with You, but many are the stations between us. * I wonder at him who says, "I remember my Lord. "When someone remembers Me in him self, I remember him in Myself; and when someone remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than his.

**The sincere.**

It was at the time of the construction of the Ka‘bah that Abraham and Ishmael prayed for a prophet to be born among the people of Makkah. The prayer was answered, and the coming of the final prophet, whose focus would be Makkah, was decreed. As for the sincere—they needed no further proof, but even the conclusiveness of this sign was not enough to silence those who gave no thought to God. If one day you pass by the street of the Haqiqah and remember Him in your secret core, you will see "What no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what has never passed into the heart of any mortal.

153.text:
"O believers! Seek comfort in patience and prayer." opens with a call to the believers, and it names the two means of comfort in a single line. The word comfort is the thing sought, and the sentence names where it is found, in patience and in prayer. The verse does not offer comfort apart from these two. "Allah is truly with those who are patient" closes the verse with the promise that the Lord keeps company with the patient. The word truly confirms the promise and makes it a matter of certainty. The Jalālayn gives the sense of seeking help regarding the Hereafter through patience and prayer. The Mukhtaṣar reads the verse as a command to ask for help through patience and prayer, and it states that Allah gives the patient His support. The Maʿārif commentary takes the method to consist in turning to patience and prayer, and it treats patience as the ground on which the rest of the trials are met. The Tazkirul commentary states that there is only one way to succeed in the trials of life, and it is the way of those who do not waver from the path. The reader is asked to see the verse as a short rule for the believer in a time of trial: turn to patience and prayer, and hold to the nearness of the Lord that comes with them.

**Seek comfort in patience and prayer.**

O you who believe seek help regarding the Hereafter through patience in obedience and afflictions and prayer He singles it out for mention on account of its frequency and its greatness; surely God is with the patient helping them. (O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness) to fulfil the obligations of Allah and to abstain from contraventions and shameful works (and prayer) and with abundant supererogatory prayers at night and during the day in order to come clean from sin. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Messenger, ask for help from Allah in everything, through the beauty of patience and by establishing the prayer in the way Allah has instructed.

**Allah is with the patient.**

(Lo! Allah is with the steadfast) He helps, and protects the steadfast from shameful works. For that reason God most high said yet give good tidings to the patient [2:155] followed by Upon those rest blessings ṣalawāt and mercy from their Lord [2:157].

**Patience as a method.**

And the method consists in turning to patience and prayers; for Allah assures us here that He is with those who are patient. As to how Sabr can save man from all kinds of trouble and pain and resolve all his difficulties, the secret has been revealed in the last phrase of this verse - "Surely, Allah is with those who are patient. Seek the help of [God's] blessing ṣalāt through patience.

**One way to succeed.**

There is only one way to succeed in the trials of life, and that is through patience and prayer. Those who do not waver from the path despite all the difficulties it presents—who stay with God even when no worldly benefit seems to accrue therefrom—are the ones who will finally emerge successful from the trials of life. But it is those who lose all for God’s sake who are the true finders; it is those who give their lives for Him who inherit life everlasting. One who has adopted religion in the real sense of the word has truly discovered God.

**Religion in the real sense.**

In the terminology of Holy Qur'an and the Hadith, Al-Sabirun is the title of those who are steadfast in observing all the three forms with equal rigour. Let us not forget that, according to the Hadith, whenever the Holy Prophet $ was faced with a grave problem of any kind, he always hastened to offer nail prayers, and through the barakah (benediction) of the prayers Allah came to his aid and resolved the problem satisfactorily. After Allah commanded that He be appreciated, He ordained patience and prayer. It is said that the patient are entitled to the ultimate treasures and the highest ranks inasmuch as they have attained the company maʿiyya of God most high who said Surely God is with maʿa the patient.

154.text:
"Never say that those martyred in the cause of Allah are dead, in fact, they are alive!" opens with a prohibition, and the word never closes off a common way of speaking about the dead. The people addressed are the believers, and the term martyred is the one that the verse uses for those who fell in the cause of Allah. The second half of the sentence turns on the word fact, and the exclamation shows that the matter is not to be doubted. "But you do not perceive it" closes the verse with the limit of the listeners' own sight. The reader is told that the life of these people is real, though it is beyond what the living can perceive. The Mukhtaṣar reads the verse as a command not to call those killed in the way of Allah dead. The Tanwīr gives the sense that these are living like those who are close to their Lord, while the hypocrites were speaking of the dead as lost. The Maʿārif commentary takes the martyr as one who is treated as living in the matters of the grave, and it sets out the view that the bodies of the martyrs are described as living while the world treats them as dead. The Tazkirul commentary states that peace and happiness will be complete for those who were tested in God's service. The reader is asked to hold the verse as a correction to a way of speaking that the believers were to give up.

**Never say they are dead.**

And say not of those slain in God’s way that ‘They are dead’; rather they are living their spirits are according to a hadīth contained in green birds that take wing freely wherever they wish in Paradise; but you are not aware but you do not know their condition. Do not say, O believers, about those who are killed whilst striving in Allah’s path that they are dead just as others are; rather, they are alive with their Lord, but you do not realise that they are living, because the way in which they are alive can only be understood through revelation from Allah. (And call not those who are slain in the way of Allah) in obedience of Allah, on the Day of Badr or in any other battle ( " dead ") like any other dead people.

**In fact, they are alive.**

(Nay they are living) they are rather living like those living in Paradise, being provided with comfort and bounties, (only ye perceive not) you are not aware of the honour bestowed upon them or of their real state. The life of this world has left them behind, but they have reached endless life.12 What have they lost by being released from this world's abasement? But peace and happiness will materialize in their complete form only in the next eternal world.

**You do not perceive it.**

It is a fact that the servant is either enjoying a bounty that he should be thankful for, or suffering a calamity that he should meet with patience. They have reached union with the exaltedness of the Patron. They are, therefore, reported as living and we are forbidden to call them dead. However, for all worldly purposes they are treated at par with the dead; their properties are divided and their wives can remarry.

**The martyr in the grave.**

One who dies in the cause of Allah is a Shahid (Martyr) and, although, it is correct and even allowed to call him "dead", yet we are forbidden to regard their death like ordinary deaths. If, in spite of Ahadith, the body mingles with earth (what, in fact, has made the author of Ruh al-Ma ani doubt is how can, in spite of Ahadith, the body of a Shahid be eaten away by earth) the explanation would be that according to Hadith the body would not return to dust; however, it does not deny the process of decay and decomposition caused by other factors like geo-chemical reaction, body enzymes, and bacteria. Imam Ahmad reported that 'Abdur-Rahman bin Ka'b bin Malik narrated from his father that Allah's Messenger said: This world being a testing ground, God’s servants face obstacles in their path so that the earnest among them may be distinguished from those who are not serious and sincere.

**Lost in the sight of the world.**

Allah thereafter mentions the saying of the hypocrites apropos the martyrs of Badr, Uhud and all the other battles: " So-and-so has died and lost all comfort and happiness " , this in order to aggravate sincere believers, and so Allah says: But it is those who lose all for God’s sake who are the true finders; it is those who give their lives for Him who inherit life everlasting. God's praise be on those slain concerning whom the King says that they are alive.

155.text:
"We will certainly test you with a touch of fear and famine and loss of property, life, and crops." opens with the word certainly, which removes any doubt that the trial will come. The Lord speaks in the first person, and the trial is a test that He sets. The list of losses gives the trial its shape: fear, famine, the loss of property, the loss of life, and the loss of crops. Each is a touch of what the believers may suffer, and the word touch marks it as a measure and not a destruction. "Give good news to those who patiently endure" is the instruction that follows, and it turns the list of losses into a reason for hope. The verse ends with the good news for those who are patient, so the trial is set beside the promise. The Mukhtaṣar states that Allah will test people with different kinds of hardship, and that the Prophet is to give good news to those who are patient. The Jalālayn gives the trial as a fear of an enemy and a hunger caused by drought. The Maʿārif commentary places the verse within the theme of war with the enemy, and it sets the test of the believers against the test of the opponents. The Tazkirul commentary calls these obstacles normal and everyday, and it states that the eternal blessings of the next life are reserved for those who persevere. The reader is asked to see the verse as a test that comes with its own promise.

**We will certainly test you.**

Surely We will try you with something of fear of an enemy and hunger by way of drought and diminution of goods as a result of destruction and lives as a result of slaughter death and disease and fruits by way of crop damage that is to say We will try you to see if you practise patience or not; yet give good tidings of Paradise to the patient during calamities;. (And surely We shall try you) test you (with something of fear) fear of the enemy (and hunger) in the years of drought, (and loss of wealth and lives) through killing, death and illnesses (and crops) and the loss of crops;. Allah will test people with different types of hardships: some with fear of those who are against them; hunger because of lack of food; lack of money because of losing it or difficulty gaining it; loss of lives due to death from diseases and tragedies that kill people, or being martyred for the sake of Allah; and a lack of resources from the earth. And We will indeed try you with something of fear and hunger, and decrease of wealth, souls, and fruits; and give good news to the patient.

**Fear and famine.**

And certainly, We shall test you with something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits, but give glad tidings to As-Sabirin (the patient)Who, when afflicted with calamity, say: The frightened and the hungry persons show the effects of the affliction outwardly and this is why Allah has used here the word 'Libas' (cover or clothes) of fear and hunger. He says, "We will test you, sometimes with fear, sometimes with dread, sometimes with poverty, sometimes with hunger, sometimes with outward affliction, sometimes with inward sorrow. Then He mentioned His trial to the believer, saying:

**Loss of property, life and crops.**

Hence, He tests them with the bounty sometimes and sometimes with the afflictions of fear and hunger. These obstacles present themselves in normal, everyday situations of life—human temptations, family demands, worldly interests, social pressure—these are the things that provide the real test of life. Those verses give preference to the theme of war with infidels over other themes for two reasons: first, the sacrifice of life is a grand sacrifice; whoever steadfastly endures this loss will, undoubtedly, learn to be patient on losses of lesser magnitude; second, it is relevant to the situation too, as the objectionist on the orientation of Ka'bah had been facing it. With the tongue of his state he was saying, "In separation I make do because of shame before Your image, in union I burn in fear it will cease.

**Give good news to the patient.**

Give good news, O Prophet, to those who are patient in the face of these hardships, of what will make them happy in this world and in the Afterlife. (No Muslim is struck with an affliction and then says Istirja' when the affliction strikes, and then says: 'O Allah! Reward me for my loss and give me what is better than it,' but Allah will do just that.) I will restrict myself here, to presenting the considered and the very balanced view of my worthy teacher Maulana Ashraf Ali of Than a Bhawan; incidentally, his view is in close conformity with the teachings of the Holy Qur'an, as also, those of the Holy Prophet . God has reserved the eternal blessings of the next life for those who show themselves willing to sacrifice this life for the next.

**Trials and the next life.**

Those who do not waver from the path despite all the difficulties it presents—who stay with God even when no worldly benefit seems to accrue therefrom—are the ones who will finally emerge successful from the trials of life. But it is those who lose all for God’s sake who are the true finders; it is those who give their lives for Him who inherit life everlasting. For, though, life in Barzakh is given to' everybody which gives him perception of reward and punishment but Shahid in the Barzakh life is qualitatively different from the one given to other persons.
