If, in spite of Ahadith, the body mingles with earth (what, in fact, has made the author of Ruh al-Ma ani doubt is how can, in spite of Ahadith, the body of a Shahid be eaten away by earth) the explanation would be that according to Hadith the body would not return to dust; however, it does not deny the process of decay and decomposition caused by other factors like geo-chemical reaction, body enzymes, and bacteria.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Earlier, alluding to an unpleasant incident, patience and steadfastness were inculcated and the excellence of Sabirun (the patient people) was mentioned. The next verses mention, in some detail, other unpleasant incidents and culminate in describing the excellence of pa-tience, and perseverance in it.

156.text:
"Who, when faced with a disaster, say, Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we will all return." opens with a description of the patient, the people who are glad to be given good news. The phrase when faced with a disaster names the moment of the test, and the answer comes at that moment. The words Surely to Allah we belong give the first part of the reply, and the belonging is to the Lord. "and to Him we will all return" completes the reply with the return to the Lord, so the whole of the answer is set in the two directions of belonging and return. The verse is a short creed spoken in the hour of loss. The Mukhtaṣar takes the patient as those who, when they are struck by one of these trials, say that they belong to Allah and return to Him. The Jalālayn gives the example of a man whose lamp was put out, and who made the same reply. The Maʿārif commentary states that the patient people used to recite this formula, and it treats the quality of patience as varying from one person to another. The Tazkirul commentary states that man is required to pass through all these tests and trials, and that death brings every person to stand face to face with his Lord. The reader is asked to see the verse as the words that the patient speak at the moment of loss.

**Who, when faced with a disaster.**

those who when they are struck by an affliction a calamity say ‘Surely we belong to God we are His possession and servants with whom He does as He pleases; and to Him we will return’ in the Hereafter whereupon He will requite us in one hadīth it is said that ‘whoever pronounces the istirjā‘ sc. the formula ‘surely we belong to God and to Him we will return’ when an affliction befalls him God will reward him and compensate him with what is better’. The patient are those who, when they are struck by one of these hardships, say, in acceptance, that all power belongs to Allah, He deals with us as He wills, and we will return to Him on the Day of Judgement, and it is He Who created us and showers us with many blessings; so, to Him is our return and our end. Those who when they are struck by an affliction face the matter with patience and even gratitude. (No Muslim is struck with an affliction and then says Istirja' when the affliction strikes, and then says: 'O Allah! Reward me for my loss and give me what is better than it,' but Allah will do just that.)

**Surely to Allah we belong.**

That the patient people used to recite: ‌ : 'We belong to Allah and to Him we are to return' is, in fact, an inculcation of the principle of virtue. Similarly it is said that on one occasion when his lamp blew out the Prophet s uttered the istirjā‘ whereupon ‘Ā’isha said to him saying ‘But it is just a lamp’ to which he replied ‘Whatever bothers a believer is an affliction of sorts’ this is reported by Abū Dāwūd in his section on mursal reports. Surely We will try you with something of fear and hunger and diminu tion of goods and lives and fruits; yet give good tidings to the patient; those who when they are struck by an affliction say Surely we belong to God and to Him we will return. And certainly, We shall test you with something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits, but give glad tidings to As-Sabirin (the patient)Who, when afflicted with calamity, say:

**And to Him we will all return.**

’ All of a sudden, death will bring you standing face to face with God, at which time you will be held accountable for all your deeds. The Prophet Muhammad said that when a man dies, everything connected with him is cut off except three things: The nature and the significance of the severe test man is put to by Allah has been thoroughly discussed while explaining the verse’ ‌ ‌ 'And when his Lord put Ibrahim to a test'. But a prior knowledge of such accidents makes it easier to bear them and be patient about them.

**Degrees of patience.**

But as the quality and degree of patience varies from person to person, everyone will be rewarded individually according to and commensurate with his quality of patience. Whoever is patient with the misfortunes of near relations will have recompense and stations of nearness qurubāt. Hence, He tests them with the bounty sometimes and sometimes with the afflictions of fear and hunger. The frightened and the hungry persons show the effects of the affliction outwardly and this is why Allah has used here the word 'Libas' (cover or clothes) of fear and hunger.

**Tests and the day of return.**

The Prophet Muhammad said, ‘People are asleep, they will wake up only when they die. Man is required to pass in all these tests and trials by leading a need-based life rather than a desire and greed-based life, so that in the life hereafter, God will allow him to enter Paradise, to live there forever in close proximity to his Creator. (but give) O Muhammad (glad tidings to the steadfast, who say, when a misfortune) like the ones I have mentioned (striketh them: lo! We are Allah's) we are the slaves of Allah (and lo! Unto Him we are returning) after we die; and if we are not pleased with His decree, He will not be pleased with our works. The Prophet Muhammad said that when a man dies, everything connected with him is cut off except three things:

**What else the same passage holds.**

"Truly, to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return. They are those on whom are the Salawat (i.e., who are blessed and will be forgiven) from their Lord, and (they are those who) receive His mercy, and it is they who are the guided ones The Believer is Patient with the Affliction and thus gains a Reward Whatever their magnitude, accidents are unnerving. Since the entire Ummah is addressed here, the Ummah should realize that the world is a place of hardships and labour; it is a place of ordeal. It will not, therefore, amount to impatience if one does regard such accidents as either strange or a remote chance. And as the Ummah, generally, displays the spirit of patience in all its deeds, the reward of Mercy is common to everyone who strives to be patient. The suggestion is that this is what the patient people should say as it brings excellent reward, relieves from the burden of sorrow and suffering and consoles effectively the grieved heart.

157.text:
"They are the ones who will receive Allah's blessings and mercy." opens with the reward that follows the patience of the verse before. The phrase the ones who will receive names the people who have been described, and it attaches the blessings and mercy to them. The blessing and the mercy are both named, so the reward has two parts. "And it is they who are rightly guided" closes the verse with the guidance that these people have. The word rightly makes the guidance a sure one, and the phrase it is they places the guidance on those who were described. The verse is short, and its weight is in the naming of the people who are blessed and guided. The Mukhtaṣar states that those who possess these virtues are praised by Allah, and that they are the ones guided to the path of truth. The Tanwīr reads the guidance as the act of remembering that the affliction comes from the Lord. The Maʿārif commentary repeats its point about the nature of severe trials, and it observes that patience is easier for those who know the trial will come. The Tazkirul commentary describes those who persevere until the end as the ones who reach the goal. The reader is asked to see the verse as the reward set beside the trial, with the guidance as the sign of who has received it.

**Blessings and mercy.**

Upon those rest blessings forgiveness and mercy grace from their Lord and those — they are the truly guided to rectitude. Upon those rest blessings and mercy from their Lord and those-they are the truly guided. (Such) those who have these traits (are they on whom are blessings) forgiveness (from their Lord) in this world, (and mercy) in that they are not tormented in the Hereafter. Those who possess these virtues are praised by Allah in the highest gathering of angels, and mercy descends on them.

**Those who will be guided.**

(And such are they who are rightly guided) to remember that we are Allah's and unto Him we shall return. They are those on whom are the Salawat (i.e., who are blessed and will be forgiven) from their Lord, and (they are those who) receive His mercy, and it is they who are the guided ones. Because He blessed them in the beginning lammā raḥimahum fī l-bidāya they were guided in the end ihtadaw fī l-nihāya.

**Patience before the reward.**

The nature and the significance of the severe test man is put to by Allah has been thoroughly discussed while explaining the verse’ ‌ ‌ 'And when his Lord put Ibrahim to a test'. But a prior knowledge of such accidents makes it easier to bear them and be patient about them. It will not, therefore, amount to impatience if one does regard such accidents as either strange or a remote chance. But as the quality and degree of patience varies from person to person, everyone will be rewarded individually according to and commensurate with his quality of patience.

**Calamity and the words of faith.**

(Who, when afflicted with calamity, say: "Truly, to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return.") meaning, those who recite this statement to comfort themselves in the face of their loss, know that they belong to Allah and that He does what He wills with His servants. The frightened and the hungry persons show the effects of the affliction outwardly and this is why Allah has used here the word 'Libas' (cover or clothes) of fear and hunger. (No Muslim is struck with an affliction and then says Istirja' when the affliction strikes, and then says: 'O Allah! Reward me for my loss and give me what is better than it,' but Allah will do just that.) They attained their patience and their ability to withstand the demands of the divine decree from His prior blessings to them.

**Perseverance to the end.**

If one persists in the service of God, finally reaching a stage where there is nothing but burning sand beneath one’s feet, then God in His mercy will cause a refreshing spring to gush forth from the dryness of the desert sands. They were prevented from believing in him by the fear that if they accepted an Arab prophet, their religious hegemony would come to an end. They deemed it wise to conceal the truth, for they thought that they would lose their worldly status were they to accept it; but it would have been much wiser for them to have proclaimed it. Only those who persevere in their disbelief till the day they die will be deprived of His mercy.

158.text:
"Indeed, the hills of Ṣafa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah." opens with a statement that the two hills are among the marks that Allah has set. The word symbols is the key, since the hills are named as signs of the worship and not as sacred in themselves. The phrase among the symbols places them in a group of marks that the Lord has made known. The verse goes on with the rule that follows from the symbols, and the rule gives the reason the believers may go between them. The verse continues, "So whoever performs the pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage, let them walk between the two hills." "And whoever does good willingly" follows, and it closes with "Allah is truly Appreciative, All-Knowing." The sentence is one of the few in the passage that names a place as a sign, so the reader is asked to see the place through the sign it carries. The Mukhtaṣar states that whoever goes to the Kaʿba to perform the acts of Hajj or ʿUmrah is not to be blamed for going between the two hills. The Tanwīr reads Allah as mentioning the dislike of the believers for going between them, and it states that there is no transgression in doing so. The Jalālayn places the two hills near Makkah and treats the pacing between them as a pillar of the rite in the view of some scholars. The Wāḥidī commentary gives the occasion, in which the believers asked the Messenger about the matter after Islam came. The Tazkirul commentary links the hills to Hājar, who ran back and forth between them in distress. The reader is asked to see the verse as the start of a rule that answers a question about an older custom.

**The symbols of Allah.**

Truly ṣafā and Marwa are among the symbols of God These sites and relics tilka al-mashāhidu wa-l-rusūm these ruins and remains wa-tilka al-aṬlālu wa-l-ruqūm are extolled and visited. Whoever goes to the Kaaba to perform the acts of Hajj or Umrah, there is no fault in them walking between the two mountains. (Lo! Al-Safa and al-Marwah) going around al-Safa and al-Marwah (are among the rites of Allah) among the rites of pilgrimage that Allah, Exalted is He, has commanded.

**No sin in going between them.**

(It is therefore no sin) one commits no transgression (for him who is on pilgrimage to the House or visiteth it, to go around them (as the pagan custom is). And he who doeth good of his own accord) and whoever performs extra works other than this obligation of going between al-Safa and al-Marwah, (Lo! Allah is Responsive) accepts such works, (Aware) of your intentions; it is also said that this means: By clarifying that there was no fault in this action, Allah was comforting those Muslims who avoided walking between the mountains because they feared it was an unacceptable action from the time of ignorance before Islam; but Allah made it clear that the walking between the mountains was an acceptable act of Hajj. So it is not a sin on him who performs Hajj or 'Umrah (pilgrimage) of the House to perform Tawaf between them. Truly Safā and Marwa two mountains near Makkah are among the waymarks sha‘ā’ir plural of sha‘īra of God the ritual ceremonies of His religion so whoever makes the Pilgrimage to the House or the Visitation that is whoever prepares to perform the Pilgrimage hajj or the Visitation ‘umra the original sense of both terms hajja and i‘tamara is ‘to aim for’ and ‘to visit’ respectively; he would not be at fault it would not be a sin if he circumambulates them the original tā’ of yatatawwafa ‘circumambulate’ has been assimilated with the tā’ by pacing quickly sa‘y between them seven times this was revealed when the Muslims were averse to this circumambulation because the pagan Arabs used to circumambulate them and there was an idol atop each mountain which they used to stroke.

**Hajar and the hills.**

Acting at God’s behest, he took his wife Hajar and his infant son Ishmael, and left them in the place now known as Makkah. Distressed, she ran back and forth between the hills of Safa and Marwah. When Muslims perform the pilgrimage to Makkah, they repeat Hajar’s historic quest between these hills, thus commemorating the profound relevance of the event to everyone who struggles in the path of God. And that is only because Umayma walked beside it in a group [of women] trailing a garment. so whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or the visitation he would not be at fault if he circumambulates them; and whoever volunteers good God is Grateful Knowing. ṣafā and Marwa were favored by being close to the House.

**The occasion of the question.**

When Islam came, they asked Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, about this, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse . Before Islam, they used to make pilgrimage to Manat and were forbidden from going between al-Safa and al-Marwah. When they went to pilgrimage with Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, they mentioned this to him. We disliked going in between al-Safa and al-Marwah, because they were the shrines of Quraysh in the pre-Islamic period, and so we abandoned them in Islam.

**Pilgrimage and its sense.**

Lexically, Hajj means to aim, to intend; while, in the terminology of the Qur'an and Hadith, the act of deciding to go solely on a pilgrimage of the House of Allah and performing required rites while there, is called the Hajj. Lexically, Umrah means ziyarah or pilgrimage; while, in the terminology of the Shari'ah, the visit to al-Masjid al-Haram and the doing of tawaf and Sayee there is called Umrah. Al-Shāfi‘ī and others however considered it to be a pillar of the Pilgrimage rituals. The Prophet made clear its obligatory aspect when he said that ‘God has prescribed for you the pacing sa‘y’ as reported by al-Bayhaqī and others; and he the Prophet also said ‘Begin with what God has begun’ meaning al-Safā as reported by Muslim; and whoever volunteers tatawwa‘a a variant reading is yattawa‘ the ta’ here being assimilated good that is any good deed such as circumambulation or other that is not obligatory on him; God is Grateful for such a deed and rewards that person for it Knowing it.

**What else the same passage holds.**

The subject of the Ka'bah as we would do well to recollect, started all the way back from Verse 124 : 'And when his Lord put Ibrahim to a test', later opening with the statement that the Ka'bah was made a place for repeated convergence, a sanctuary, and a centre of divine worship as ordained (Verse 125). It is reported from Ibn ‘Abbās that this pacing between the two is not obligatory based on the fact that when no sin can be incurred the context implies free choice. Then came the famous prayer of Sayyidna Ibrahim in which he requested Allah Almighty that he and his people be initiated into the correct method of performing the manasik the required rites, or acts of worship (126 - 129); which is inclusive of the Hajj and Umrah. We can now see that the centrality of the House of Allah as the place of worship has been expressed manifestly when it was declared to be the Qiblah the direction and orientation of all Salah no matter where it is performed; while at the same time, the importance of the House of Allah was established when it was made the objective in the performance of the Hajj and Umrah. The present verse opens with the solemn declaration that the two hills, Safa and Marwah adjoining the Ka'bah in Makkah, are tangible signs from Allah. Pilgrims walk briskly between them after they have made the tawaf of the Holy Ka'bah .

159.text:
"Those who hide the clear proofs and guidance that We have revealed, after We made it clear for humanity in the Book." opens with the group who conceal, and the sentence states the offence in full. The sentence ends with "will be condemned by Allah and all those who condemn," so the charge is followed at once by the condemnation of Allah and of all who condemn in turn. The clear proofs and the guidance are named together, so both the signs and the way they lead are hidden. The phrase after We made it clear for humanity in the Book shows that the matter was plain in the Book itself, which makes the concealment harder to excuse. The verse does not name the group in this sentence, but the earlier verses have described the People of the Book, and the reader is shown the same people in the new charge. The Jalālayn states that the verse was revealed concerning the Jews. The Wāḥidī commentary gives the occasion as the scholars of the People of the Book. The Mukhtaṣar identifies those Jews and Christians who hide the clear proofs. The Tanwīr reads the proofs as the commands, the prohibitions, and the rest of what the Book contains. The Maʿārif commentary treats the verse as a warning to scholars who keep knowledge from the common people, and it sets out the difference between concealment and an honest silence. The reader is asked to see the verse as a charge made on the clear basis of the Book itself.

**Those who hide the proofs.**

The following was revealed concerning the Jews Those who conceal from people the clear proofs and the guidance that We have revealed such as the ‘stoning’ verse and the description of Muhammad after We have shown them clearly in the Scripture the Torah — they shall be cursed by God that is He will move them far away from His mercy and by the cursers the angels believers or by every single thing when they supplicate that they be cursed. Those Jews and Christians who hide the clear proofs which Allah revealed showing the truth of the Prophet and what he brought, after Allah had made it clear to the people in their scriptures, Allah removes them from His mercy; and all the angels, the prophets and people call for them to be removed from His mercy. Those who conceal the clear proofs and the guidance that We have revealed after We have shown them clearly in the scripture-they shall be cursed by God and by those who curse This verse alludes to those to whom the Real has unveiled knowledge of the good manners ādāb of traveling but who have become stingy in revealing [this knowledge] to aspirants [who seek] advice and guidance. (Those who hide the proofs) the commands, prohibitions and the signs mentioned in the Torah (and the guidance) i.e. the description given there of Muhammad ﷺ and his feature (which We revealed) exposited, (after We had made it clear) to the Children of Israel (in the Scripture) in the Torah:

**Made clear in the Book.**

This was revealed about the scholars of the people of the Book and their concealment of the verse of stoning [the adulterers who are married] and the matter of Muhammad, Allah bless him and give him peace. One fears for them that the blessing will be removed from their knowledge when they fall short in it just as they held back in imparting [that knowledge] to the deserving. Verily, those who conceal the clear proofs, evidences and the guidance, which We have sent down, after We have made it clear for the People in the Book, they are the ones cursed by Allah and cursed by the cursers Except those who repent and do righteous deeds, and openly declare (the truth which they concealed). This will not be considered as 'concealment of knowledge' since what is not allowed is the concealment of clear guidance given in the Qur'an and Sunnah which it is rather necessary to disclose and disseminate widely.

**The Companions and the Hadith.**

It may be noted that the verse in question warns those who may conceal what has been revealed in the Holy Qur'an; it does not mention Hadith as such. But, the blessed Companions ruled that the Hadith of the Holy Prophet was covered under this reference to the Qur'an and that is why they thought that concealing the Hadith would also put them under this warning. This is supported by a hadith from the blessed Companion, Bard' ibn Azib where the Holy Prophet has been reported to have said that the word al-la inun ('those who curse') refers to all animal life that moves on the earth. Abu Al-'Aliyah said that these Ayat, "were revealed about the People of the Scripture who hid the description of Muhammad .

**Whoever hides knowledge.**

(Whoever was asked about knowledge that one has, but he hid it, then a bridle made of fire will be tied around his mouth on the Day of Resurrection.) (and cursed by the cursers) means that the angels and the believers will curse them. It may be noted that the verse in question warns those who may conceal what has been revealed in the Holy Qur'an; it does not mention Hadith as such. This will not be considered as 'concealment of knowledge' since what is not allowed is the concealment of clear guidance given in the Qur'an and Sunnah which it is rather necessary to disclose and disseminate widely.

**Creator and the purpose of the world.**

He is the only worthy focus of man’s attention. Our very existence on earth, and all the benefits we derive from the world around us, are manifestations of His unbounded grace and mercy. In return, we should become God’s devoted servants, living for Him, dying for Him, and setting all our hopes on winning His eternal favour. If he becomes conscious of this, his Lord will mean everything to him, as a mother means everything to her infant.

**What else the same passage holds.**

As part of the debated issue of Qiblah several verses earlier, the text has pointed out how the people of the Book went about concealing the truth concerning the prophethood of the Holy Prophet for whom the Ka'bah was appointed as the Qiblah . "Those whom We have given the Book recognize him (The Holy Prophet) as they recognize their own sons. And, in fact, a group of them does conceal the truth while they know." Now the text, in order to conclude the subject, warns those who not only conceal the truth but, going further ahead in obstinacy, persist in their effort.

160.text:
"As for those who repent, mend their ways, and let the truth be known" opens with the exception to the charge of the verse before. The word repent names the turning back from the deed, and the three acts that follow show what repentance calls for: mending the ways, and letting the truth be known. The sentence does not stop at sorrow, since the truth must also be made known. "they are the ones to whom I will turn in forgiveness" is the promise that follows, so the Lord is the one who turns. The verse is brief, and its exception is wide enough to include any who make these three moves. The Mukhtaṣar takes the exception as those who repent to Allah and ask for forgiveness, and it states that the Lord turns to those who turn to Him. The Tanwīr reads the mending of the ways as a turning away from Judaism and the making of amends. The Qushayrī commentary treats the making of amends as the showing of the goodness in the action. The Maʿārif commentary sets the warning of the text against the senseless persistence in concealment, and it treats the exception as the way back. "for I am the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful" gives the reason for the promise, so the door is open to any who come to it. The reader is asked to see the verse as a door left open after the charge.

**Repentance and amends.**

Except those that repent turning back from such deeds and make amends in their actions and show clearly what they were concealing — them I shall turn relenting accepting their repentance; I am the Relenting the Merciful to believers. (Except such of them as repent) from Judaism (and amend) worship Allah alone without ascribing to Him any partners (and make manifest) the traits and description of Muhammad. The exception is those who repent to Allah, asking for forgiveness, and regretting having hidden these clear signs, correcting what they do outwardly and inwardly, and making clear the truth and guidance which they had hidden. Except those that repent and make amends and show clearly-them I shall turn [relenting]; I am the Relenting the Merciful. [Except those who] compensate for their past negligence by graciously turning back taking on the task of giving advice to the aspirants.

**The Lord turns to those who turn.**

He turns to those who turn to Him, asking for forgiveness and regretting what they have done, and He forgives and is compassionate with them. (These it is towards whom I relent) overlook their past transgressions. And I am the One Who accepts repentance, the Most Merciful Verily, those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers, it is they on whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, combined They will abide therein (under the curse in Hell), their punishment will neither be lightened nor will they be reprieved. (I am the Relenting) towards those who repent, (the Merciful) towards him who dies in a state of repentance.

**Showing the truth.**

They show clearly to [the aspirants] the goodness in upholding certain modes of behavior explaining and demonstrating this to them in a beautiful way. Surely the clearest proof of the clarity of your actions and the truest tes timony of that by which you call people to God is that your behavior does not contradict what you have alluded to in your speech. God most high said And I do not desire to be inconsistent in what I forbid you [11:88]. Now the text, in order to conclude the subject, warns those who not only conceal the truth but, going further ahead in obstinacy, persist in their effort.

**Persistence in concealment.**

The ultimate fate of this senseless persistence being all too obvious, Allah Almighty still extends the promise of His mercy and forgiveness to those who repent and reflect on what they did, retrace their steps and correct their negative attitude towards divine truth and, in order to demonstrate their positive stand, come forward and state the truth clearly and publicly. Do you want them to deny Allah and His Messenger ?' For, anything beyond their comprehension would breed doubts in their minds and the possibility is there that they may refuse to accept it. The Ayah (2:159 above) states that those who hide the knowledge will be cursed, (in this life and) on the Day of Resurrection, by Allah, the angels, all humanity, and those who curse (including the animals) each in its own distinct way. "Those whom We have given the Book recognize him (The Holy Prophet) as they recognize their own sons.

**A world turned toward its Lord.**

He is the only worthy focus of man’s attention. Our very existence on earth, and all the benefits we derive from the world around us, are manifestations of His unbounded grace and mercy. In return, we should become God’s devoted servants, living for Him, dying for Him, and setting all our hopes on winning His eternal favour. If he becomes conscious of this, his Lord will mean everything to him, as a mother means everything to her infant.

161.text:
"Surely those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers are condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity." opens with the word surely, which confirms the sentence that follows. The verse turns from the exception in the verse before to the fate of those who die in disbelief. The condemnation is named as coming from three sides: from Allah, from the angels, and from all of humanity. The three sources give the curse its weight, so that no one stands on the side of the condemned. The sentence is the start of the account of their fate, and the verse before had left the way of repentance open. The Mukhtaṣar states that those who disbelieve and die in disbelief, having not turned, are the ones who receive this condemnation. The Maʿārif commentary takes the phrase that the disbelievers die while they are disbelievers as the point of the verse, and it sets out what the word curse means in the sense of removing a person from the mercy of the Lord. The Qushayrī commentary treats the phrase upon them the curse as the mark of those who are sent away. The Tazkirul commentary links the curse to the choice of a life that the Lord does not reward. The reader is asked to see the verse as a sentence that the open door of the verse before has been placed against.

**Those who disbelieve and die.**

But those who disbelieve and die disbelieving wa-hum kuffār ‘they being disbelievers’ is a circumstantial qualifier — upon them shall be the curse of God and the angels and of people altogether that is they deserve such a curse in this life and in the next; ‘people’ here is said to be either people in general or believers. (Lo! Those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers) in Allah and His Messenger; (on them is the curse of Allah) the torment of Allah (and of the angels) the curse of the angels (and of men combined) the curses directed by believers towards each other will end up as curses on these unbelievers. Those who disbelieve and die in disbelief, not having repented, they are condemned by Allah by being removed from His mercy; and the angels and people all call for them to be removed and excluded from Allah’s mercy. But those who disbelieve and die disbelieving-upon them shall be the curse of God and the angels and of people altogether.

**Condemned by Allah.**

Verily, those who conceal the clear proofs, evidences and the guidance, which We have sent down, after We have made it clear for the People in the Book, they are the ones cursed by Allah and cursed by the cursers Except those who repent and do righteous deeds, and openly declare (the truth which they concealed). And I am the One Who accepts repentance, the Most Merciful Verily, those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers, it is they on whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, combined They will abide therein (under the curse in Hell), their punishment will neither be lightened nor will they be reprieved. Mujahid said, "When the earth is struck by drought, the animals say, 'This is because of the sinners among the Children of Adam. The Ayah (2:159 above) states that those who hide the knowledge will be cursed, (in this life and) on the Day of Resurrection, by Allah, the angels, all humanity, and those who curse (including the animals) each in its own distinct way.

**The angels and humanity.**

From the words of the text :'and died while they were disbelievers', commentators al-Jassas, al-Qurtubi and some others have formulated the view that it is not permissible to curse an infidel about whom it is not certain that he is to die in a state of infidelity. Common people in Muslim societies seem to neglect this aspect of standard Muslim behaviour, specially our Muslim sisters who are prone to use very hard language about those they do not like among the circle of their acquaintances. It should be clearly understood that the act of cursing becomes effective not only by using the word, 'curse' but all synonyms used are subject to the same ruling. The word 'La nah ' (curse) means: to remove away from the mercy of Allah Almighty'.

**The companions of separation.**

Here the allusion is to those who after they have traveled the path of spiritual desire irāda find it fitting to return to the states of the people of habit ahl al-ʿāda.261 Then while they are in the grip of this estrange ment [from the path] and in this condition [they] leave the world. Those are the companions of separation aṣḥāb al-furqa. Abiding therein: the chastisement shall not be lightened for them no respite shall be given them. If he becomes conscious of this, his Lord will mean everything to him, as a mother means everything to her infant.

**Life without reward.**

He is the only worthy focus of man’s attention. Our very existence on earth, and all the benefits we derive from the world around us, are manifestations of His unbounded grace and mercy. In return, we should become God’s devoted servants, living for Him, dying for Him, and setting all our hopes on winning His eternal favour. (Lo! Those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers) in Allah and His Messenger; (on them is the curse of Allah) the torment of Allah (and of the angels) the curse of the angels (and of men combined) the curses directed by believers towards each other will end up as curses on these unbelievers.

162.text:
"They will be in Hell forever." opens with the duration of the sentence, which is given as forever. The verse does not add a limit to the fire, so the word forever stands as the first fact of their state. "Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be delayed from it." The two negatives close off the two hopes that a sinner might keep, which are relief and delay. The punishment is fixed, and no lessening or postponement is offered. The verse follows the condemnation of the verse before, and its two negatives make the sentence complete. The Mukhtaṣar states that they will always be condemned and that their punishment will not be lightened. The Tanwīr reads the abiding as abiding in the curse, and it reads the doom as one that will not be lightened for them. The Maʿārif commentary repeats the point about the word curse, and it treats the phrase they died while they were disbelievers as the point at which the sentence is fixed. The reader is asked to see the verse as the close of the sentence on those who die in disbelief.

**Forever in Hell.**

Abiding therein that is in the curse and the Fire the latter indicated by the following words the chastisement shall not be lightened for them not even for a blink of an eye no respite shall be given them in which to have time to repent or to excuse themselves. (They ever dwell therein) i.e. in this curse. They will always be condemned, and their punishment will not be lightened, not even for a day; and they will not be given any extra time on the Day of Judgement. Abiding: that is they remain forever in their contemptible position insignificant and [find no] lessening of it or relief without kindness or favors.

**The punishment not lightened.**

(The doom will not be lightened for them) it will not be lifted or reduced, (neither will they be reprieved) their torment will not be deferred. (it is they on whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, combined. They will abide therein (under the curse in Hell).) But those who disbelieve and die disbelieving-upon them shall be the curse of God and the angels and of people altogether. There is no drawing near for their spirits or setting straight their calamity no asking for mercy from anyone.

**Concealment and the curse of the earth.**

Mujahid said, "When the earth is struck by drought, the animals say, 'This is because of the sinners among the Children of Adam. This Ayah refers to those who regret what they have been doing and correct their behavior and, thus, explain to the people what they have been hiding. And I am the One Who accepts repentance, the Most Merciful Verily, those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers, it is they on whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, combined They will abide therein (under the curse in Hell), their punishment will neither be lightened nor will they be reprieved. It should be clearly understood that the act of cursing becomes effective not only by using the word, 'curse' but all synonyms used are subject to the same ruling.

**The curse and its meaning.**

From the words of the text :'and died while they were disbelievers', commentators al-Jassas, al-Qurtubi and some others have formulated the view that it is not permissible to curse an infidel about whom it is not certain that he is to die in a state of infidelity. Common people in Muslim societies seem to neglect this aspect of standard Muslim behaviour, specially our Muslim sisters who are prone to use very hard language about those they do not like among the circle of their acquaintances. The word 'La nah ' (curse) means: to remove away from the mercy of Allah Almighty'. Here the allusion is to those who after they have traveled the path of spiritual desire irāda find it fitting to return to the states of the people of habit ahl al-ʿāda.261 Then while they are in the grip of this estrange ment [from the path] and in this condition [they] leave the world.

**The curse of the angels.**

He is the only worthy focus of man’s attention. Our very existence on earth, and all the benefits we derive from the world around us, are manifestations of His unbounded grace and mercy. In return, we should become God’s devoted servants, living for Him, dying for Him, and setting all our hopes on winning His eternal favour. If he becomes conscious of this, his Lord will mean everything to him, as a mother means everything to her infant.

163.text:
"Your God is only One God." opens with the Lord named as one, and the word only is placed on the oneness itself. The verse does not share the name of God with any other, and the sentence makes the unity its first claim. "There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful." The second sentence takes the oneness to its ground: no god is worthy of worship but He, and the two names that close the verse are the names of mercy. The Mukhtaṣar begins with the address to the people, and it states that the Allah of the people is the true Allah, the One, unique in His being. The Tanwīr reads the verse as a declaration of the oneness of God, without son or partner. The Maʿārif commentary takes the sentence as a reply to the mushrikīn of Arabia, who asked the Prophet to describe his Lord, and it treats the claim as one that needs proof. The Qushayrī commentary asks who was there before the apportioning but the One. The Tazkirul commentary calls God the only worthy focus of human attention. The reader is asked to see the verse as the first and simplest statement of the faith, given with the mercy that makes the oneness a source of hope.

**Your God is only One God.**

(Your God is one God) without son or partner; (there is no God save Him, the Beneficent) the Tender, (the Merciful) the Compassionate. O people, your Allah is the true Allah, the One, unique in His essence and attributes. And your Ilah is One Ilah (God Allah), La ilaha illa Huwa (there is none who has the right to be worshipped but He), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. On the day of apportioning, who was there but He, the One?

**No god worthy of worship but Him.**

There is no other true god, and He is the Merciful and His mercy is vast. He is One in claiming the right of being worshipped, that is, in view of the nature of His Being, the comprehensiveness of His most perfect attributes and the great charisma of His creation and its nurture, all human obedience, all ibadah all worship has to be for Him alone.

**The Most Compassionate and Most Merciful.**

He is the Most Gracious Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful Ar-Rahim. He is Compassionate with His creation, surrounding them with many blessings. He is the only worthy focus of man’s attention. Before the day of apportioning who was there?

**The question of the mushrikīn.**

When they asked him Muhammad to describe his Lord the following was revealed Your God the One deserving of your worship is One God without any equal in either essence or attribute; there is no god except Him He is the Compassionate the Merciful. When the mushrikin (the associators) of Arabia heard the verse 'And your god is one God', all against their own belief, they were puzzled thinking how could there be just one single object of worship for the whole wide world. If this was a serious claim, there has to be some proof in support. He is One in the state of His being, that is, there exists in the universe of His creation no entity like Him.

**Before the apportioning.**

There were no tracks and no traces, there was no one in the house. Allah then declares His Oneness because the unbelievers denied this divine Oneness, saying: Our very existence on earth, and all the benefits we derive from the world around us, are manifestations of His unbounded grace and mercy. In return, we should become God’s devoted servants, living for Him, dying for Him, and setting all our hopes on winning His eternal favour.

**What else the same passage holds.**

That proof has been tersely encased in the present two verses.

164.text:
"Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth" opens the verse with a sign that the believers are asked to look at. The sign is the making of the sky and the earth, and the sentence turns the whole visible world into a book to be read. The list that follows names the alternation of the day and the night, and the ships that sail the sea for the benefit of humanity. "The rain sent down by Allah from the skies, reviving the earth after its death" gives the sign of life returned to a dead land. "The scattering of all kinds of creatures throughout" the earth is the next sign, followed by "the shifting of the winds" and "the clouds drifting between the heavens and the earth." The verse closes with "in all of this are surely signs for people of understanding," which gathers the list into one judgement about the people who reflect. The Mukhtaṣar calls these clear signs of the oneness of Allah. The Tanwīr reads the sign as the proof of the divine oneness, and it reads the clouds as subservient between heaven and earth. The Qushayrī commentary gives the sense that the Lord shows the generality of His signs in this verse. The Tazkirul commentary states that the signs spread over the universe serve as a reminder to those who think. The Maʿārif commentary takes the ships on the sea as one of the signs of the Lord's care for people. The reader is asked to see the verse as a call to read the world as the sign of the One God. The reader is also reminded that the same signs are set before people who think, so each sentence of the verse is a question put to the listener about what he has seen with his own eyes.

**Creation of the heavens and the earth.**

(Lo! In the creation of the heavens and the earth) i.e. in their making; or as it is said: in the making of what is in them, (and the difference of night and day) in the alternation of night and day, and in the increase and decrease of their duration, (and the ships which run upon the sea with that which is of use to men) in their livelihoods, (and the water) rain (which Allah sendeth down from the sky, thereby reviving) through rain (the earth after its death) after suffering by drought and being dried up, (and dispersing) creating (all kinds of beasts) male and female (therein, and the ordinance of the winds) in changing the direction of the wind towards the right and towards the left, coming sometimes from the East and sometimes from the West, sometimes carrying torment and sometimes mercy: Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of the night and the day, the ships that run on the sea with what benefits people, the water that God sends down from heaven giving life to the earth after its death, the scattering of every beast therein, the shifting of the winds, the clouds subjected between heaven and earth-there are signs for a people who have intellect. The following are clear signs of the Oneness of Allah, glory be to Him, for those who understand the evidence and proof: the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the wonders in them; the succession of night and day; the passing of life and death; happiness and sorrow; wealth and poverty; ships that sail through the waters of the sea, carrying food, clothing, trade and other things that people need and which benefit them; water that Allah sends down, bringing the earth to life with the agriculture and pasture that grows in it, and the living creatures He spreads out in it; the changing of the winds from one direction to another; and the clouds, controlled between the sky and the earth.

**Day, night, and the ships.**

Similarly, the movement of boats on the surface of waters, is a formidable indicator of Allah's power which gave water, a substance so liquid and fluid, the property of lifting on its back ships which carry tons and tons of weight all the way from the East to the West. The existence of a limitless world in the form of the earth and the heavens is a proof that there must be a Creator behind it. Then the fact that every single thing benefits the rest of the universe, in some manner or the other, shows that all things have been designed according to a definite and absolutely conscious plan.

**Rain that revives the earth.**

Therefore, the sky, with its height, intricate design, vastness, the heavenly objects in orbit, and this earth, with its density, its lowlands, mountains, seas, deserts, valleys, and other structures, and beneficial things that it has. (And no moving (living) creature is there on earth but its provision is due from Allah. And He knows its dwelling place and its deposit (in the uterus or grave). All is in a Clear Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz the Book of Decrees with Allah).)(11:6) (and the clouds obedient) subservient (between heaven and earth) He says: in all these (are signs) indications of the Lord's divine Oneness (for people who have sense) who believe that they are from Allah. Even if this fluidity of sea-surface was there, help from winds was still needed in order to cover all those thousands of nautical miles across the seas of the world.

**Scattering of living creatures.**

There are many books about the wind rain, stars and the regulations related to them, but here is not the place to elaborate on that, and Allah knows best. In this verse the Lord of the Universe shows the generality of people the road to Himself, so that they will gaze upon the wonders of the dominion of heaven and earth and on the artisanries of land and sea and then recognize the Artisan and attest to His oneness. The elect among the faithful know the attributes and from the attributes reach the Object of attribution and from the name the Named. Apparently lifeless objects are invested with life through a natural process: this shows that death is only a temporary phase in this universe.

**Signs for the thoughtful.**

Then He mentioned the sign of His divine Oneness, saying: Now in Verse 164, there is a series of signs and proofs in support of the premise that Allah Almighty is really One. But these signs, spread all over the universe, serve as proofs of God’s existence and His role as sustainer of the entire universe, only to one who sincerely reflects on these signs. They look from Him to Him, not from the other to Him.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Stated simply, these can be grasped by the learned and the ignorant alike. How can one bypass the wonder of the creation of the heavens and the earth? Who can ignore the constant alternation of the night and the day? Their origination and their perpetuity is the work of His perfect power alone and that there is absolutely no being other than Him who can take that credit. Then, there is the movement of winds which Allah harnesses into the service of man, and in His wisdom, keeps changing their direction. These are great signs; they tell us that they were created and operated by a supreme being, the One who is All-Knowing, All-Aware, All-Wise. If the substance of water was not given a state in which the molecules move freely among themselves while remaining in one mass, a functional fluidity in other words, all this maritime activity would not be there. The Holy Qur'an has summarized the subject by saying: "If He wills, He can still the winds, then, ships shall remain standing on the back of the seas. The use of the expression :'with what benefits men' points out to the countless benefits that accrue to human beings when they mutually trade their goods through sea freighters. It is interesting to keep in mind the variations these benefits take from country to country and from age to age. Then comes the marvel of water descending from the sky, drop by drop, released in a measure and manner that it hurts nothing. If it always came in the form of a flood, nothing would have survived, man or animal or things.

165.text:
"Still there are some who take others as Allah's equal" opens with the word still, which turns from the signs of the verse before to the error of those who rivals of the Lord. The people are described as taking others as equals to Allah, and the verse names the act of making peers. "They love them as they should love Allah." The love given to these peers is the love that belongs to the Lord, so the verse names the error in the terms of love. "But the true believers love Allah even more." The sentence sets the believers apart by the greater love they give to Allah. "If only the wrongdoers could see the horrible punishment awaiting them, they would certainly realize that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is indeed severe in punishment." The last clause turns to the future sight of the wrongdoers, and it closes on the truth that all power is the Lord's. The Mukhtaṣar states that those who have real faith love Allah more than those others, and that if the wrongdoers could see with their own eyes they would not worship anyone with Him. The Tanwīr reads the verse as a passage on the love of the unbelievers for their idols. The Maʿārif commentary treats the verse as pointing out the error of those who attach themselves to other things. The Tazkirul commentary states that this happens when ordinary human beings see someone and give that person the love that is owed to God. The reader is asked to see the verse as a diagnosis of misplaced love, and a warning that the sight of the punishment will come too late.

**Take others as Allah's equal.**

(Yet of mankind) i.e. the unbelievers (are some who take unto themselves) who worship (rivals to Allah) idols, (loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah) like the love that sincere believers have for Allah (-Those who believe are stauncher) more lasting (in their love for Allah) than are the unbelievers vis-�-vis their idols; it is also said that this verse was revealed about the hypocrites who buried their gold and silver or hid it in caves; and it is also said that this means: they took their leaders as gods (-that those who do evil had but known) if only the idolaters knew, (when they behold the doom) on the Day of Judgement, (that power) and might and invincibility (belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment!) in the Hereafter-if they knew this, they would certainly have believed in this world. Even with these clear signs, there are people who take others besides Allah as their gods, considering them equal to Him, and loving them as they love Allah. Among the people are some who take peers apart from God, loving them as if loving God. Now the present verse points out to the error made by those who associate others in the divinity of Allah and think that they are caretakers of their needs.

**They love them as they should love Allah.**

But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else). (But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else) Their attachment to them reaches the proportions of love that is due for Allah alone. It necessarily entails that all one’s feelings of love and devotion become exclusively reserved for that being or object.

**The true believers love Allah even more.**

Those who have real faith love Allah more than those others love their gods: they do not worship anyone besides Him; and they love Him in hardship and in ease, while those others only love their gods when things are going well – when things go badly, they call on Allah alone. (But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else) If their love for their object of wor ship is real, why do they turn away from it toward another? In direct contrast to this profile of the polytheists, there are the true believers who love Allah alone, and very staunchly too, for a poly-theist may turn away from his self-made god in the event of an impending loss, but a true believer reposes his total confidence in Allah, in gain and loss alike, retaining His love and pleasure as his lasting possession, never leaving his Creator whatever the odds against him be.

**If only the wrongdoers could see.**

If the wrongdoers could see with their own eyes the punishment that waits in the Afterlife for those who worship others with Allah and commit sins, then they would know that all power belongs to Allah alone and that He is firm in punishing those who stubbornly rebel. (...and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them.) meaning, when they see Allah's torment, their power and means of salvation are all cut off, and they will have no way of making amends, nor will they find a way of escape from the Fire. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about: This Ayah means: 'If we only had a chance to go back to the life so that we could disown them (their idols, leaders, etc.) shun their worship, ignore them and worship Allah Alone instead.' But they utter a lie in this regard, because if they were given the chance to go back, they would only return to what they were prohibited from doing, just as Allah said. If this were the only verse in the whole Qur'an about the faithful and God's friends, their eminence and honor would be complete, for the Lord of the Worlds is saying, "They love Me intensely and more completely than the unbelievers love their objects of worship.

**Misplaced love in the world.**

This happens when ordinary human beings, seeing someone surrounded by visible pomp and splendour, are impressed by certain special talents or qualities; when they find certain individuals occupying ‘seats’ sanctified by centuries-old traditions; when at times they are impressed by the large following which certain people enjoy and when they see public figures surrounded with the halo of mysterious legends. But the truth is that in this universe of God, no one save God possesses any power or greatness. They think that they are clinging to a firm rock which will surely help them in the Hereafter. Then, when they can, they take down the wooden one and make another from silver or gold.

**What else the same passage holds.**

In the verses that appeared earlier, there was a strong and positive view of Allah's Oneness. And of mankind are some who take (for worship) others besides Allah as rivals (to Allah). The general meaning of the verse then is ‘If they were aware in this world of the severity of God’s chastisement and of the fact that power is God’s alone the moment they come to see it with their own eyes on the Day of Resurrection they would not take to themselves compeers’. If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them), and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them And those who followed will say: "If only we had one more chance to return (to the worldly life), we would disown (declare ourselves as innocent from) them as they have disowned (declared themselves as innocent from) us. " Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them. And they will never get out of the Fire The Condition of the Polytheists in this Life and the Hereafter Now, returning back to the 'unjust', the Holy Qur'an makes a subtle suggestion that the opportunity to correct their position was there; they could have recognized through their frustrations with their gods that they were helpless and that real power rested with Allah. In these Ayat, Allah mentions the condition of the polytheists in this life and their destination in the Hereafter. But, they missed the opportunity and must now learn the hard way.

166.text:
"Consider the Day when those who misled others will disown their followers" opens with the call to consider a day, and the scene is one in which the leaders who misled others disown those who followed them. The disowning is set against the leading that came before, so the sentence turns the old bond into a separation. "when they face the torment and the bonds that united them will be cut off" gives the moment of the separation. The bonds that held them together are named as the thing that will be cut, and the torment is what brings the cutting. The verse is placed after the warning about the disbelievers who follow forefathers, so the scene is the end of that following. The Mukhtaṣar states that the leaders who were followed in disbelief will reject those who followed them. The Qushayrī commentary states that when they see the beginnings of the chastisement, the ones who were followed declare themselves quit of their followers. The Maʿārif commentary takes the people of the leaders as the ones who will see this scene, and it treats the deeds they see as a cause of anguish. The Tanwīr reads the disowning as the leaders disowning those who were lowly. The Tazkirul commentary links the urge to worship God to human nature, and it observes that man's going astray does not mean he abandons God. The reader is asked to see the verse as the day on which every false bond is broken, and every false leader stands alone.

**Consider the Day.**

When idh here substitutes for the previous idh those who were followed that is the leaders disown their followers that is to say when they have denied misleading them the latter and they have seen the chastisement and the cords the bonds of affection and kinship that were between them on earth are cut away before them from them taqatta‘at ‘cut away’ is a supplement to tabarra’a ‘disown’. Towards the end of the preceding verse it was said that the punishment of the Hereafter is severe. Then the leaders who were followed in disbelief will reject the weak people who followed them because of seeing the terrors and hardships of the Day of Judgement; so, all ties and means of escape will be cut off from them. (When those who were followed) the leaders (disown those who followed (them) the lowly among people, (and they behold) both the leaders and the lowly (the doom) in the Hereafter, (and all their aims) the pledges and congeniality that were between them in this world (collapse with them).

**The followers disowned.**

When those who were followed declare themselves quit of those who followed them. ("Glorified be You! You are our Wali (Lord) instead of them. Nay, but they used to worship the Jinn; most of them were believers in them.")(34:41) (And they have taken (for worship) alihah (gods) besides Allah, that they might give them honor, power and glory (and also protect them from Allah' punishment). Nay, but they (the so-called gods) will deny their worship of them, and become opponents to them (on the Day of Resurrection).)(19:81-82) Prophet Ibrahim said to his people: When the so-called 'people' of their leaders will see this turnabout of theirs, they will fret and fume but will be unable to do anything about it except wishing that there be a return for them to the mortal world where they could, at least, square up with their greasy leaders - 'May be this time they come back to us seeking our allegiance which would be a perfect time to say no to them and to distance ourselves from them and to do to them what they did to us.'.

**The bonds cut off.**

Hence, when they see the beginnings of the chastisement at the resurrection, they will know that they have no place on which to stand and will disown the idols. As for the faithful, their friendship is the fruit of the Real's friend ship-as He says, "He loves them, and they love Him" [5:54]. (...and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them.) meaning, when they see Allah's torment, their power and means of salvation are all cut off, and they will have no way of making amends, nor will they find a way of escape from the Fire. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about: The severity of the punishment against which the polytheists have been warned will unfold itself when their leaders whom they followed will disown them as their votaries; and they both, the leaders and the led, will witness the punishment, and whatever bonds of leading and following may have existed between them would be snapped apart, very much like it happens in our mortal world when people share in the illegal but wriggle out when apprehended, so much so, that they would even go to the limit of refusing to recognize their accomplices!

**Their deeds seen as anguish.**

They are stuck with 'their deeds which they see as remorse', and they all, the leaders and their followers, 'are not to come out from the Fire', since the punishment for shirk, the grave sin of associating partners with Allah, is to remain in the Fire for ever. This Ayah means: 'If we only had a chance to go back to the life so that we could disown them (their idols, leaders, etc.) shun their worship, ignore them and worship Allah Alone instead.' But they utter a lie in this regard, because if they were given the chance to go back, they would only return to what they were prohibited from doing, just as Allah said. Therefore the steep roads and trials that come to them do not bring any defect into their love, so they do not turn away from the Real. (When those who were followed) the leaders (disown those who followed (them) the lowly among people, (and they behold) both the leaders and the lowly (the doom) in the Hereafter, (and all their aims) the pledges and congeniality that were between them in this world (collapse with them).

**The urge to worship God.**

The urge to worship God is so integral to human nature that no one can live without Him. Man’s going astray does not mean that he abandons God altogether. That is why the Islamic law holds unlawful all those things which, in any degree, lead to deviation, i.e. diverting man’s natural desire for God in some other direction. Satan encourages human beings to channelise their feelings of awe and reverence on to different paths in order that their attachment to God may be weakened.

167.text:
"The misled followers will cry, If only we could have a second chance, we would disown them as they disowned us." opens with the cry of the followers, who ask for a return to the world. The second chance is the thing they long for, and their wish is to answer the leaders in the same coin, by disowning them as they were disowned. The cry is given in full, so the reader hears their hope before the answer comes. "And so Allah will make them remorseful of their misdeeds." The reply is the Lord's, and it returns the cry to the misdeeds of those who speak it. "And they will never be able to leave the Fire." The Maʿārif commentary takes the severity of the punishment as the subject, and it sets this scene against the sight of the leaders. The Tanwīr reads the anguish as their own deeds shown to them. The reader is asked to see the verse as a wish that comes too late, and a sentence that is not reversed.

**If only we could have a second chance.**

And those who followed say ‘O if only we might return again to the world and disown them the ones who had been followed as they have disowned us!’ on this day the particle law ‘if only’ is an optative and its response is natabarra’a ‘we disown’. The weak and those who followed will say, ‘If only we could go back to the earth, we would reject our leaders as they reject us’. This Ayah means: 'If we only had a chance to go back to the life so that we could disown them (their idols, leaders, etc.) shun their worship, ignore them and worship Allah Alone instead.' But they utter a lie in this regard, because if they were given the chance to go back, they would only return to what they were prohibited from doing, just as Allah said.

(Thus will Allah show them their own deeds as anguish) as regrets (for them) in the Hereafter, (and they) the leaders and those who followed them (will not emerge from the Fire). Allah shows them the severe punishment in the Afterlife and the consequence of following their leaders in falsehood: regrets and sorrow, and they will never leave the fire of Hell. So God shall show them their works anguish for them! How severe it will be is now the subject of the present verse.

Never shall they exit from the Fire once they have entered it. So just as He showed them the severity of His chastisement and their disowning of one another so too God shall show them their evil works as anguish hasarāt is a circumstantial qualifier regrets for them! At that time they will know the bitter taste of the companionship of created things but they will not be able to attain anything but anguish. The severity of the punishment against which the polytheists have been warned will unfold itself when their leaders whom they followed will disown them as their votaries; and they both, the leaders and the led, will witness the punishment, and whatever bonds of leading and following may have existed between them would be snapped apart, very much like it happens in our mortal world when people share in the illegal but wriggle out when apprehended, so much so, that they would even go to the limit of refusing to recognize their accomplices!

When the so-called 'people' of their leaders will see this turnabout of theirs, they will fret and fume but will be unable to do anything about it except wishing that there be a return for them to the mortal world where they could, at least, square up with their greasy leaders - 'May be this time they come back to us seeking our allegiance which would be a perfect time to say no to them and to distance ourselves from them and to do to them what they did to us.'. (...and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them.) meaning, when they see Allah's torment, their power and means of salvation are all cut off, and they will have no way of making amends, nor will they find a way of escape from the Fire. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about: They are stuck with 'their deeds which they see as remorse', and they all, the leaders and their followers, 'are not to come out from the Fire', since the punishment for shirk, the grave sin of associating partners with Allah, is to remain in the Fire for ever. (And they have taken (for worship) alihah (gods) besides Allah, that they might give them honor, power and glory (and also protect them from Allah' punishment). Nay, but they (the so-called gods) will deny their worship of them, and become opponents to them (on the Day of Resurrection).)(19:81-82) Prophet Ibrahim said to his people:

**the lowly and those who followed.**

(And those who were but followers) i.e. the lowly (will say: If a return) to this world (were possible for us, we would disown them) disown the leaders in this world (even as they have disowned us) in the Hereafter. ("Glorified be You! You are our Wali (Lord) instead of them. Nay, but they used to worship the Jinn; most of them were believers in them.")(34:41) That is why the Islamic law holds unlawful all those things which, in any degree, lead to deviation, i.e. diverting man’s natural desire for God in some other direction. The polytheists set certain animals free in the name of their deities.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Towards the end of the preceding verse it was said that the punishment of the Hereafter is severe. And of mankind are some who take (for worship) others besides Allah as rivals (to Allah). But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else). If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them), and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them And those who followed will say: "If only we had one more chance to return (to the worldly life), we would disown (declare ourselves as innocent from) them as they have disowned (declared themselves as innocent from) us.

168.text:
"O humanity! Eat from what is lawful and good on the earth and do not follow Satan's footsteps." opens with the address to all people, which is wider than the address to the believers. The command is to eat from what is lawful and good on the earth, and the limit is set in the same breath: do not follow the footsteps of Satan. "He is truly your sworn enemy." The verse names the enemy in a single phrase, and the word truly confirms the enmity. The verse is placed after the warning about the forefathers, and it turns to what the people may eat. The Mukhtaṣar states that the people should eat from the meat, vegetables, and fruits of the earth, and that they should not follow the actions of Satan. The Tanwīr reads the lawful as what is not the property of another and the wholesome as what is clean. The Maʿārif commentary takes the word tayyib as good in the sense that includes the clean. The Qushayrī commentary treats what is lawful, even when it is disliked at present, as lawful in its own right. The Wāḥidī commentary gives the occasion, which concerned Thaqīf and Khuzāʿa and others who set apart the animals they had named. The Tazkirul commentary states that the real God is replaced by a false one when people set up rules of their own. The reader is asked to see the verse as the start of a rule on food that is also a warning about obedience to Satan.

**O humanity.**

The following was revealed when some said that it was unlawful to take a camel that has been let loose sawā’ib O people eat of what is in the earth lawful halālan is a circumstantial qualifier and wholesome tayyiban is an adjective for emphasis that is to say what is delicious; and follow not the steps the ways of Satan meaning what he embellishes of temptations; he is a manifest foe to you whose enmity is clear;. O people, eat from the meat, vegetables and fruits of the earth which are lawful and good, and not harmful. O people eat of what is in the earth lawful and wholesome; and fol low not the steps of Satan; he is a manifest foe to you; That which is forbidden even if it is pleasing now is contaminated in the end. (Lo! He is an open enemy for you) whose enmity towards you is quite manifest.

**Eat from what is lawful and good.**

(Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome) that is not prohibited by Allah (in the earth) of what is cultivated in lands and of cattle, (and follow not the footsteps of the devil) the embellishments and whisperings of the devil concerning the unlawfulness of the cultivation of land and of raising cattle. " The word (tayyib) means 'good' as inclusive of the clean and the pure and covers the twin aspects of being lawful, permissible or halal and being naturally desirable. That which is permitted even if it is hateful now is wholesome in the end. In that sense, what has been made halal means that a knot has been opened and the restriction has been removed.

**Do not follow Satan's footsteps.**

Do not follow the actions of Satan and his evil whisperings: he is a clear enemy who is hostile to you – anyone with sense would not follow an enemy who wants to harm and mislead them. Verily, he is to you an open enemy He (Satan) commands you only what is evil and Fahsha' (sinful), and that you should say about Allah what you know not. (Lo! He is an open enemy for you) whose enmity towards you is quite manifest. ('Every type of wealth I have endowed My servants is allowed for them...' (until), 'I have created My servants Hunafa' (pure or upright), but the devils came to them and led them astray from their (true) religion and prohibited them from what I allowed for them. ')

**Forbidden by one's own rule.**

This was revealed about Thaqif, Khuza'ah and Amir ibn Sa'sa'a who forbade themselves certain foods and meats. They forbade the Bahirah, al-Sa'ibah, al-Wasilah as well as al-Hamiyah . Why go about making things unlawful on your own which is a grave sin, and when it is dedicated to someone other than Allah it becomes impure and what is impure is unlawful. If anyone dedicates an animal to anyone other than Allah out of ignorance or carelessness and wishes to make amends, he should resolve to retreat from his misdeed and repent on what he did, in which case, the meat of that animal will become lawful for him.

**The real God replaced.**

It is the worship of something other than God in order to satisfy one’s feelings of devotion and veneration. What actually happens is that the real God is replaced by a false god. That is why the Islamic law holds unlawful all those things which, in any degree, lead to deviation, i.e. diverting man’s natural desire for God in some other direction. Satan encourages human beings to channelise their feelings of awe and reverence on to different paths in order that their attachment to God may be weakened.

**What else the same passage holds.**

Eat of that which is lawful and good on the earth, and follow not the footsteps of Shaytan (Satan). The real meaning of the root word (halla) in (halalan tayyiban: The Order to eat the Lawful Things, and the Prohibition of following the Footsteps of Shaytan The blessed Companion Sahl ibn Abdullah has said: "Salvation depends on three things - eating halal fulfilling (Divine) obligations and following the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet . The word (khutuwat) is the plural form of (khutwah) which is the distance between the two feet when striding. Here the khutuwat of Shaytan means Satanic deeds. Polytheistic practices, such as releasing animals in the name of idols or dedicating them, whether big or small, to a saint or to anyone other than Allah has been declared unlawful in Verse 173 which follows. The present Verse is not negating the unlawfulness of such an animal as wrongly conceived by some people. The objective of the verse is to stress that animals which Allah has made lawful should not be made unlawful by dedicating them to idols. Let them be what they are and use them for personal benefit.

169.text:
"He only incites you to commit evil and indecency" opens with the word only, which limits the work of Satan to evil and indecency. The verb incites marks the way in which he works on people, through suggestion and not through force. "And to claim against Allah what you do not know" names the worst of his commands, which is to speak about the Lord without knowledge. The verse moves from the harm of evil and indecency to the harm of speaking falsely about God. The sentence is short, and the two parts together show the path of Satan from the act to the claim. The verse is the continuation of the call to eat what is lawful, so the command to avoid Satan's path is shown in the sphere of food and of speech. The Mukhtaṣar states that Satan commands harmful and evil actions and disobedience. The Tanwīr reads the devil as the one who enjoins the evil. The Jalālayn gives the sense that he commands evil, sin, and indecency. The Maʿārif commentary treats the word su' as something that bothers a person, and it sets out the Satanic suggestion as the cause of disobedience. The Tazkirul commentary links the diluting of man's natural feelings of reverence to the work of Satan. The reader is asked to see the verse as an account of how Satan leads people into what they do not know.

**He only incites you.**

he only commands you to evil sin and indecency what is abhorred by the Law and that you should speak against God what you do not know such as forbidding what He has not forbidden and otherwise. Satan only commands harmful, evil actions and disobedience that will bring hardship, as well as for you to say things about faith in Allah and His sacred laws that have not been given to you by Allah or His Prophet. the devil (enjoineth upon you only the evil) evil works (and the foul) transgressions, (and that ye should tell) lies (concerning Allah that which ye know not).

**Evil and indecency.**

(He (Satan) commands you only what is evil and Fahsha (sinful), and that you should say about Allah what you know not.) The verse means: 'Your enemy, Satan, commands you to commit evil acts and what is worse than that, such as adultery and so forth. The word ‘su' in means something which bothers somebody good and reasonable. The Satanic suggestion has the effect of bringing forth the expedient gains in evil deeds and thereby opening the avenues of negating the truth, while the angelic suggestion promises reward and success for good deeds and leaves the happy effect of a heart in peace at its attestation of the truth."

**To claim against Allah what you do not know.**
